title.raw: 卷23 志第18 五行下 Volume 23 Treatises 18: Five Elements 2

sentences.zh: 序《洪範五行傳》曰：「視之不明，是謂不知。

translations.literal: The preface to the Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When vision is not clear, this is called not knowing.'
translations.idiomatic: The preface to the Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "When sight is dim, it is called ignorance."

sentences.zh: 厥咎舒，厥罰常燠，厥極疾。

translations.literal: Its fault is laxity; its punishment is constant heat; its extreme is illness.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is slackness; the penalty is unrelenting heat; the ultimate consequence is disease.

sentences.zh: 時則有草妖，時則有羽蟲之孽。

translations.literal: At such times there are grass demons; at such times there are calamities of winged insects.
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons grass-spirits appear, and calamities wrought by winged creatures arise.

sentences.zh: 故有羊禍，故有目疾，有赤眚赤祥。

translations.literal: Therefore there are sheep portents; therefore there are eye ailments, red disasters and red omens.
translations.idiomatic: Hence come sheep omens, eye afflictions, and baleful red signs.

sentences.zh: 惟水沴火。

translations.literal: Only water harms fire.
translations.idiomatic: Water alone overcomes fire.

sentences.zh: 」常燠後齊天保八年三月，大熱，人或暍死。

translations.literal: 'Constant heat'—afterward, in the third month of the eighth year of Tianbao of Northern Qi, there was great heat, and some people died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: As for "constant heat": in the third month of Northern Qi's Tianbao year 8, the heat was extreme, and people died of sunstroke.

sentences.zh: 劉向《五行傳》曰：「視不明，用近習，賢者不進，不肖不退，百職廢壞，庶事不從，其過在政教舒緩。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When vision is not clear, employing close favorites, the worthy are not advanced, the unworthy are not removed, the hundred offices are ruined, and the myriad affairs are not followed—the fault lies in lax government and teaching.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's Wuxing Commentary says: "When a ruler's sight is clouded, he relies on those near at hand; the worthy are not promoted, the unworthy are not dismissed; every office falls into ruin and nothing is properly managed—the fault lies in slack governance and instruction."

sentences.zh: 」時帝狂躁、荒淫無度之應。

translations.literal: 'At that time it was the response of the emperor's frenzy, wildness, and boundless debauchery.
translations.idiomatic: This was Heaven's response to an emperor's frenzy, recklessness, and boundless debauchery.

sentences.zh: 草妖高祖時，上黨有人，宅後每夜有人呼聲，求之不得。

translations.literal: Grass demon—during Gaozu's reign, in Shangdang there was a man whose behind his house every night there were voices calling; he searched but could not find them.
translations.idiomatic: Grass-spirit omen: During Emperor Gaozu's reign, a man in Shangdang heard voices calling every night behind his house, yet however he searched, he could find no one.

sentences.zh: 去宅一里所，但見人參一本，枝葉峻茂。

translations.literal: One li from the house, he only saw one ginseng plant, its branches and leaves luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: About a li from his home he found only a single ginseng plant, its branches and leaves towering and lush.

sentences.zh: 因掘去之，其根五尺餘，具體人狀，呼聲遂絕。

translations.literal: He dug it out; its root was more than five chi, fully in human form, and the calling voices then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When he dug it up, the root was more than five chi long and shaped like a human being—and the calling voices stopped.

sentences.zh: 蓋草妖也。

translations.literal: This was probably a grass demon.
translations.idiomatic: It was evidently a grass-spirit omen.

sentences.zh: 視不明之咎。

translations.literal: The fault of unclear vision.
translations.idiomatic: This was the penalty for clouded royal sight.

sentences.zh: 時晉王陰有奪宗之計，諂事親要，以求聲譽譖皇太子，高祖惑之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Jin secretly harbored a plan to seize the succession, flattered those close to the emperor, sought reputation, and slandered the crown prince; Gaozu was deluded by this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Jin secretly plotted to seize the succession, fawning on the emperor's intimates and trading on his reputation to slander the crown prince—and Gaozu was taken in.

sentences.zh: 人參不當言，有物憑之。

translations.literal: Ginseng should not speak; some thing possessed it.
translations.idiomatic: Ginseng ought not to speak; some entity had possessed it.

sentences.zh: 上黨，黨與也。

translations.literal: Shangdang—dang means faction.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdang: dang means "faction."

sentences.zh: 親要之人，乃党晉王而譖太子。

translations.literal: Those close to the emperor were a faction for the Prince of Jin and slandered the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's intimates formed a faction backing the Prince of Jin and defaming the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 高祖不悟，聽邪言，廢無辜，有罪用，因此而亂也。

translations.literal: Gaozu did not understand, listened to evil words, deposed the innocent, employed the guilty, and thereby came disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu failed to see the truth, heeded slander, deposed the innocent and empowered the guilty—and disorder followed.

sentences.zh: 羽蟲之孽梁中大同元年，邵陵王綸在南徐州，坐廳事。

translations.literal: Calamity of winged insects—in the first year of Datong of Liang, Prince of Shaoling Lun was at Southern Xuzhou, seated in the reception hall.
translations.idiomatic: Winged-creature calamity: In Liang's Datong year 1, Prince Shaoling Xiao Lun was sitting in his reception hall in Southern Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 有野鳥如鳶數百，飛屋樑上，彈射不中。

translations.literal: There were several hundred wild birds like kites that flew onto the roof beams; shooting and slinging could not hit them.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred wild birds resembling kites alighted on the roof beams; neither bow nor sling could bring them down.

sentences.zh: 俄頃失所在。

translations.literal: In a moment they vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later they disappeared.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「野鳥入君室，其邑虛，君亡之他方。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'When wild birds enter the ruler's chamber, the city will be emptied, and the ruler will flee to another region.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When wild birds enter the ruler's hall, the city will be emptied and the lord will flee elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 」後綸為湘東王所襲，竟致奔亡，為西魏所殺。

translations.literal: 'Afterward Lun was attacked by the Prince of Xiangdong, and in the end fled and was killed by Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lun was attacked by the Prince of Xiangdong, fled in defeat, and was killed by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 侯景在梁，將受錫命，陳備物於庭。

translations.literal: Hou Jing was in Liang, about to receive investiture; he prepared objects in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: While Hou Jing was in Liang, about to receive formal enfeoffment, ceremonial objects were laid out in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 有野鳥如山鵲，赤嘴，集於冊書之上，鵂鶹鳥鳴於殿。

translations.literal: There were wild birds like mountain magpies, with red beaks, that gathered on the written documents; owls cried in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wild birds like mountain magpies with crimson beaks settled on the written edicts, while owls cried in the hall.

sentences.zh: 與中大同元年同占。

translations.literal: The same omen as in the first year of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as in Datong year 1.

sentences.zh: 景尋敗，將亡入海中，為羊鶤所殺。

translations.literal: Before long Jing was defeated; about to flee into the sea, he was killed by Yang Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jing was defeated; as he tried to escape by sea, Yang Kun killed him.

sentences.zh: 陳後主時，蔣山有眾鳥，鼓翼而鳴曰：「奈何帝。

translations.literal: During Chen Houzhu's reign, on Mount Jiang there were many birds that beat their wings and cried: 'What can be done, Emperor?'
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Chen's last emperor, flocks of birds on Mount Jiang beat their wings and cried, "What can be done, O Emperor?"

sentences.zh: 」京房《易飛候》曰：「鳥鳴門闕，如人音，邑且亡。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Birds cry at the gate towers in human voice—the city will soon perish.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When birds cry at the gate towers in a human voice, the city will soon fall."

sentences.zh: 」蔣山，吳之望也。

translations.literal: Mount Jiang is Wu's outlook.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Jiang was Wu's commanding vantage.

sentences.zh: 鳥于上鳴，吳空虛之象。

translations.literal: Birds crying above it is the image of Wu emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Birds crying above it foretold Wu's desolation.

sentences.zh: 及陳亡，建康為墟。

translations.literal: When Chen fell, Jiankang became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen fell, Jiankang was reduced to ruins.

sentences.zh: 又陳未亡時，有一足鳥集於殿庭，以嘴畫地成文，曰：「獨足上高臺，盛草變成灰。

translations.literal: Also before Chen fell, a one-footed bird gathered in the palace courtyard, and with its beak drew characters on the ground, saying: 'A lone foot climbs the high terrace; lush grass turns to ash.'
translations.idiomatic: Before Chen's fall, a one-footed bird appeared in the palace courtyard and traced characters on the ground with its beak: "The lone foot climbs the high terrace; lush grass turns to ash."

sentences.zh: 」獨足者，叔寶獨行無眾之應。

translations.literal: The lone foot is the response to Shubao walking alone without followers.
translations.idiomatic: "The lone foot" foretold Shubao walking alone, bereft of followers.

sentences.zh: 成草成灰者，陳政無穢，被隋火德所焚除也。

translations.literal: Grass turning to ash means Chen's government had no filth, and was burned away by Sui's fire virtue.
translations.idiomatic: "Grass turning to ash" meant Chen's rule would be consumed by Sui's fire virtue.

sentences.zh: 叔寶至長安，館于都水臺上，高臺之義也。

translations.literal: Shubao arrived at Chang'an and lodged on the Capital Water Office terrace—the meaning of the high terrace.
translations.idiomatic: When Shubao reached Chang'an, he was housed on the Capital Water Office terrace—the "high terrace" of the omen.

sentences.zh: 後齊孝昭帝即位之後，有雉飛上御座。

translations.literal: After Northern Qi Emperor Xiaozhao ascended the throne, a pheasant flew onto the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: After Northern Qi's Emperor Xiaozhao took the throne, a pheasant flew up onto the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 占同中大同元年。

translations.literal: The same omen as in the first year of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as in Datong year 1.

sentences.zh: 又有鳥止於後園，其色赤，形似鴨而有九頭。

translations.literal: Also a bird stopped in the rear garden, red in color, shaped like a duck but with nine heads.
translations.idiomatic: Another bird alighted in the rear garden—crimson, duck-shaped, but with nine heads.

sentences.zh: 其年帝崩。

translations.literal: That year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 天統三年九月，萬春鳥集仙都苑。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Tiantong, wanchun birds gathered in the Xiandu Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Northern Zhou's Tiantong year 3, wanchun birds gathered in the Xiandu Garden.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「非常之鳥，來宿於邑中，邑有兵。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'When extraordinary birds come to roost in the city, the city will have warfare.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When strange birds come to roost within a city, war will come to that city."

sentences.zh: 」周師入鄴之應也。

translations.literal: This was the response to Zhou armies entering Ye.
translations.idiomatic: This foretold the Zhou armies' entry into Ye.

sentences.zh: 武成胡後生後主初，有梟升後帳而鳴。

translations.literal: When Empress Hu bore Houzhu at the beginning, an owl flew up onto the rear canopy and cried.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Hu of Wucheng bore the future Houzhu, an owl flew up onto the rear canopy and cried.

sentences.zh: 梟不孝之鳥，不祥之應也。

translations.literal: The owl is an unfilial bird; an inauspicious response.
translations.idiomatic: The owl is the bird of unfilial piety—an omen of ill fortune.

sentences.zh: 後主嗣位，胡後淫亂事彰，遂幽後於北宮焉。

translations.literal: Houzhu succeeded to the throne; the Empress Hu's licentious conduct was exposed, and she was confined in the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu succeeded to the throne, Empress Hu's debauchery came to light, and she was imprisoned in the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 武平七年，有鸛巢太極殿，又巢并州嘉陽殿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuping, storks nested in the Hall of Supreme Polarity, and also nested in the Jiayang Hall at Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping year 7, storks built nests in the Hall of Supreme Polarity and also in Bingzhou's Jiayang Hall.

sentences.zh: 雉集晉陽宮御座，獲之。

translations.literal: A pheasant gathered on the imperial seat of the Jinyang Palace and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: A pheasant alighted on the imperial seat in the Jinyang Palace and was captured.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「鳥無故巢居君門及殿屋上，邑且虛。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'When birds for no reason nest at the ruler's gate and on hall roofs, the city will be emptied.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When birds nest without cause at the ruler's gate and on palace roofs, the city will be emptied."

sentences.zh: 」其年國滅。

translations.literal: That year the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: That year the state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 周大象二年二月，有禿鶖集洛陽宮太極殿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Daxiang of Zhou, bald ibises gathered in the Hall of Supreme Polarity of the Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Northern Zhou's Daxiang year 2, bald ibises gathered in Luoyang Palace's Hall of Supreme Polarity.

sentences.zh: 其年帝崩，後宮常虛。

translations.literal: That year the emperor died, and the rear palace was often empty.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor died, and the inner palace stood empty.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，梁主蕭琮新起後，有鵂鳥集其帳隅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, after Liang ruler Xiao Cong newly ascended, owls gathered in the corners of his canopy.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Kaihuang, after the Liang ruler Xiao Cong had newly taken the throne, owls gathered in the corners of his canopy.

sentences.zh: 未幾，琮入朝，被留于長安。

translations.literal: Before long Cong went to court and was detained at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xiao Cong went to the Sui court and was detained at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 梁國遂廢。

translations.literal: The state of Liang was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The state of Liang was abolished.

sentences.zh: 大業末，京師宮室中，恆有鴻雁之類無數，翔集其間。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, in the capital's palace halls there were constantly countless wild geese and ducks flying and gathering among them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era, countless wild geese and ducks constantly flew and gathered within the capital's palace halls.

sentences.zh: 俄而長安不守。

translations.literal: Before long Chang'an could not be held.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chang'an fell.

sentences.zh: 十三年十一月，烏鵲巢帝帳幄，驅不能止。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the thirteenth year, magpies nested in the emperor's canopy; driving them away could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of year 13, magpies nested in the emperor's canopy, and no effort could drive them away.

sentences.zh: 帝尋逢弑。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor was assassinated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 羊禍開皇十二年六月，繁昌楊悅見雲中二物，如羝羊，黃色，大如新生犬，鬥而墜。

translations.literal: Sheep portent—in the sixth month of the twelfth year of Kaihuang, Yang Yue of Fanchang saw two things in the clouds like ram-goats, yellow in color, as large as newborn dogs, fighting and falling.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep omen: In the sixth month of Kaihuang year 12, Yang Yue of Fanchang saw two cloud-born creatures like ram-goats, yellow and the size of newborn pups, fighting until one fell.

sentences.zh: 悅獲其一，數旬失所在。

translations.literal: Yue captured one; after several ten-day periods it vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Yue captured one of them; after several weeks it disappeared.

sentences.zh: 近羊禍也。

translations.literal: This was close to a sheep portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a sheep omen.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「君不明，逆火政之所致也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When the ruler is not enlightened, it is caused by violating fire governance.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "When the ruler lacks enlightenment, it comes from violating the governance of fire."

sentences.zh: 」狀如新生犬者，羔類也。

translations.literal: Shaped like newborn dogs—they are lamb kind.
translations.idiomatic: Their shape like newborn pups signified lambs.

sentences.zh: 雲體掩蔽，邪佞之象。

translations.literal: Cloud bodies covering and hiding—the image of evil flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Clouds shrouding them symbolized slanderous ministers.

sentences.zh: 羊，國姓。

translations.literal: Sheep is the surname of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep was the dynastic surname.

sentences.zh: 羔，羊子也。

translations.literal: Lamb is a young sheep.
translations.idiomatic: A lamb is a young sheep.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇既升儲貳，晉王陰毀而被廢黜。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong had already been established as heir; the Prince of Jin secretly slandered him and he was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong had already been installed as heir, but the Prince of Jin secretly undermined him and he was deposed.

sentences.zh: 二羔鬥，一羔墜之應也。

translations.literal: Two lambs fighting, one lamb falling—this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: Two lambs fighting until one fell—this was the omen fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 恭帝義寧二年，麟游太守司馬武，獻羊羔，生而無尾。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining of Emperor Gong, Sima Wu, governor of Linyou, presented a lamb born without a tail.
translations.idiomatic: In Yining year 2 of Emperor Gong, Sima Wu, governor of Linyou, presented a lamb born without a tail.

sentences.zh: 時議者以為楊氏子孫無後之象。

translations.literal: At the time commentators regarded it as an image of the Yang clan's descendants having no posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators at the time took it as a sign that the Yang clan would leave no descendants.

sentences.zh: 是歲，煬帝被殺于江都，恭帝遜位。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Yang was killed at Jiangdu, and Emperor Gong abdicated.
translations.idiomatic: That year Emperor Yang was killed at Jiangdu, and Emperor Gong abdicated.

sentences.zh: 赤眚赤祥梁天監十五年七月，荊州市殺人而身不僵，首墮於地，動口張目，血如竹箭，直上丈餘，然後如雨細下。

translations.literal: Red disaster and red omen—in the seventh month of the fifteenth year of Tianjian of Liang, in Jingzhou a man was executed but his body did not stiffen; his head fell to the ground, mouth moving and eyes opening, blood like bamboo arrows shooting upward more than a zhang, then falling like fine rain.
translations.idiomatic: Red baleful sign: In the seventh month of Liang's Tianjian year 15, at Jingzhou a executed man's body would not stiffen; his severed head fell to the ground with mouth moving and eyes open, blood shooting upward like bamboo shafts more than ten feet high, then raining down in fine drops.

sentences.zh: 是歲荊州大旱。

translations.literal: That year Jingzhou had great drought.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jingzhou suffered severe drought.

sentences.zh: 近赤祥，冤氣之應。

translations.literal: Close to red omen—the response of grievance qi.
translations.idiomatic: This was a red baleful sign—the response of aggrieved qi.

sentences.zh: 陳太建十四年三月，御座幄上見一物，如車輪，色正赤。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourteenth year of Taijian of Chen, on the imperial canopy there appeared a thing like a carriage wheel, perfectly red in color.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chen's Taijian year 14, something like a carriage wheel, bright red, appeared on the imperial canopy.

sentences.zh: 尋而帝患，無故大叫數聲而崩。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor fell ill, cried out several times for no reason, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor fell ill, cried out several times without cause, and died.

sentences.zh: 至德三年十二月，有赤物隕於太極殿前，初下時，鐘皆鳴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of Zhide, a red thing fell in front of the Hall of Supreme Polarity; when it first descended, all the bells rang.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhide year 3, a red object fell before the Hall of Supreme Polarity; as it descended, every bell rang.

sentences.zh: 又嘗進白飲，忽變為血。

translations.literal: Also once when white drink was served, it suddenly turned to blood.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, white wine that was served suddenly turned to blood.

sentences.zh: 又有血沾殿階，瀝瀝然至禦榻。

translations.literal: Also blood stained the hall steps, dripping all the way to the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: Blood also stained the hall steps, dripping all the way to the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 尋而國滅。

translations.literal: Before long the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 後齊河清二年，太原雨血。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heqing of Northern Qi, Taiyuan rained blood.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi's Heqing year 2, blood rained on Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「血者陰之精，傷害之象，僵屍之類也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: 'Blood is the essence of yin; the image of harm and injury; the kind of stiff corpses.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang said: "Blood is the essence of yin—the image of violence and harm, the mark of the slain."

sentences.zh: 」明年，周師與突厥入并州，大戰城西，伏屍百餘里。

translations.literal: The next year Zhou armies and Turks entered Bingzhou; a great battle west of the city; corpses lay for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhou armies and Turks entered Bingzhou; a great battle was fought west of the city, and corpses littered the ground for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「天雨血染衣，國亡君戮。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'When heaven rains blood that stains clothes, the state perishes and the ruler is slain.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When blood rains from heaven and stains garments, the state will fall and the ruler will be killed."

sentences.zh: 」亦後主亡國之應。

translations.literal: Also the response to Houzhu's state perishing.
translations.idiomatic: This also foretold Houzhu's loss of the state.

sentences.zh: 四年三月，有物隕於殿庭，色赤，形如數鬥器，眾星隨者如小鈴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, a thing fell in the palace courtyard, red in color, shaped like a vessel of several dou; many stars followed it like small bells.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, an object fell in the palace courtyard—red, shaped like a vessel of several dou, with many trailing stars like small bells.

sentences.zh: 四月，婁太后崩。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Empress Dowager Lou died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Empress Dowager Lou died.

sentences.zh: 武平中，有血點地，自咸陽王斛律明月宅而至於太廟。

translations.literal: During Wuping, blood spotted the ground from the residence of Prince Xianyang Hulü Mingyue to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuping era, blood spotted the ground from the residence of Prince Xianyang Hulü Mingyue all the way to the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 大將，社稷之臣也，後主以讒言殺之。

translations.literal: A great general is a minister of the altars of soil and grain; Houzhu killed him on slanderous words.
translations.idiomatic: A great general is a pillar of the state; Houzhu had him killed on the strength of slander.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，殺明月，則宗廟隨而覆矣。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: if you kill Mingyue, then the ancestral temple will follow and be overturned.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: kill Mingyue, and the ancestral temple will follow into ruin.

sentences.zh: 後主不悟，國祚竟絕。

translations.literal: Houzhu did not understand; the state's fortune was ultimately cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu failed to heed the warning, and the dynasty's fate was sealed.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「聽之不聰，是謂不謀。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When hearing is not keen, this is called not planning.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "When hearing is dull, it is called failure to deliberate."

sentences.zh: 厥咎急，厥罰寒，厥極貧。

translations.literal: Its fault is haste; its punishment is cold; its extreme is poverty.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is rashness; the penalty is cold; the ultimate consequence is destitution.

sentences.zh: 時則有鼓妖，有魚孽，有彘禍，有黑眚黑祥，惟火沴水。

translations.literal: At such times there are drum demons, fish calamities, pig portents, black disasters and black omens; only fire harms water.
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons drum-spirits appear, fish calamities arise, pig omens manifest, and black baleful signs appear—fire alone overcomes water.

sentences.zh: 」寒東魏武定四年二月，大寒。

translations.literal: 'Cold'—in the second month of the fourth year of Wuding of Eastern Wei, there was extreme cold.
translations.idiomatic: As for "cold": in the second month of Eastern Wei's Wuding year 4, the cold was extreme.

sentences.zh: 人畜凍死者，相望於道。

translations.literal: People and livestock frozen to death lined the road as far as the eye could see.
translations.idiomatic: People and livestock frozen to death lined the roads as far as the eye could see.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「誅過深，當燠而寒。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'When punishments are too deep, it should be warm but is cold.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When punishments run too deep, warmth turns to cold."

sentences.zh: 」是時後齊神武作相。

translations.literal: At that time Northern Qi's Emperor Shenwu served as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Northern Qi's Gao Huan served as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 先是爾硃文暢等謀害神武，事泄伏誅，諸與交通者，多有濫死。

translations.literal: Previously Erzhu Wenchang and others plotted to harm Shenwu; the matter was exposed and they were executed; many who had dealings with them were wrongly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Erzhu Wenchang and others had plotted against Gao Huan; when the plot was exposed they were executed, and many who had associated with them were put to death unjustly.

sentences.zh: 河清元年，歲大寒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Heqing, the year was extremely cold.
translations.idiomatic: In Heqing year 1, the cold that year was extreme.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「有德遭險，茲謂逆命。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yizhuan says: 'When the virtuous meet danger, this is called opposing fate.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the virtuous meet peril, this is called defying Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 厥異寒。

translations.literal: Its anomaly is cold.
translations.idiomatic: The anomaly is cold.

sentences.zh: 」讖曰：「殺無罪，其寒必異。

translations.literal: 'A prophecy says: 'When the innocent are killed, the cold will surely be abnormal.'
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy says: "Slay the guiltless, and the cold will be unnatural."

sentences.zh: 」是時帝淫于文宣李後，因生子，後愧恨，不舉之。

translations.literal: 'At that time the emperor debauched Empress Li of Wenxuan; she bore a son, but ashamed and resentful, she did not raise him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had an affair with Empress Li of Wenxuan; when she bore a son, ashamed and resentful, she refused to raise the child.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，於後前殺其子太原王紹德。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and before the empress killed her son, Prince of Taiyuan Shaode.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and, before the empress's eyes, killed her son Prince Shaode of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 後大哭，帝倮後而撻殺之，投于水中，良久乃蘇。

translations.literal: The empress wailed bitterly; the emperor stripped the empress naked and beat her to death, threw her into water, and after a long while she revived.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wailed in grief; the emperor stripped her naked, beat her nearly to death, and threw her into the water—only after a long while did she revive.

sentences.zh: 冤酷之應。

translations.literal: The response of cruel injustice.
translations.idiomatic: This was Heaven's response to cruel injustice.

sentences.zh: 梁天監三年三月，六年三月，並隕霜殺草。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Tianjian of Liang, and the third month of the sixth year, frost fell and killed grass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Liang's Tianjian years 3 and 6 alike, falling frost killed the grass.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「興兵妄誅，謂亡法，厥罰霜。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yizhuan says: 'Raising armies and executing wantonly is called having no law; its punishment is frost.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "To raise armies and execute wantonly is to abandon the law; the penalty is frost."

sentences.zh: 」是時，大發卒，拒魏軍于鐘離，連兵數歲。

translations.literal: 'At that time troops were massively mobilized to resist Wei armies at Zhongli; warfare continued for several years.
translations.idiomatic: At that time troops were massively mobilized to resist Wei armies at Zhongli, and fighting continued for years.

sentences.zh: 大同三年六月，朐山隕霜。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Datong, frost fell at Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Datong year 3, frost fell at Qushan.

sentences.zh: 陳太建十年八月，隕霜，殺稻菽。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the tenth year of Taijian of Chen, frost fell and killed rice and beans.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chen's Taijian year 10, frost fell and destroyed the rice and bean crops.

sentences.zh: 是時，大興師選眾，遣將吳明徹，與周師相拒于呂梁。

translations.literal: At that time armies were greatly raised and troops selected; the general Wu Mingche was sent to resist Zhou armies at Luliang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen raised large armies and dispatched General Wu Mingche to face the Zhou forces at Luliang.

sentences.zh: 鼓妖梁天監四年十一月，天清朗，西南有電光，有雷聲二。

translations.literal: Drum demon—in the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tianjian of Liang, the sky was clear; in the southwest there was lightning, and there were two thunderclaps.
translations.idiomatic: Drum-spirit omen: In the eleventh month of Liang's Tianjian year 4, though the sky was clear, lightning flashed in the southwest and two thunderclaps sounded.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「鼓之以雷霆。

translations.literal: The Changes says: 'Beat them with thunder and lightning.'
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Beat them with thunder and lightning."

sentences.zh: 」霆近鼓妖。

translations.literal: 'Thunder is close to drum demon.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder is akin to the drum-spirit omen.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「雷霆托於雲，猶君之托於人也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Thunder and lightning rely on clouds, just as the ruler relies on people.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "Thunder and lightning depend on clouds, just as the ruler depends on his people."

sentences.zh: 君不恤於天下，故兆人有怨叛之心也。

translations.literal: When the ruler does not care for the realm, therefore the common people harbor thoughts of resentment and rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler neglects the realm, the common people harbor resentment and thoughts of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，交州刺史李凱舉兵反。

translations.literal: 'That year Jiao Province Inspector Li Kai raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jiao Province Inspector Li Kai raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 十九年九月，西北隱隱有聲如雷，赤氣下至地。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the nineteenth year, in the northwest there was faint sound like thunder, and red qi descended to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year 19, a faint thunderlike sound came from the northwest, and red vapor descended to the ground.

sentences.zh: 是歲，盜殺東莞、琅邪二郡守，以朐山引魏軍。

translations.literal: That year bandits killed the prefects of Dongguan and Langye commanderies and used Qushan to lead in Wei armies.
translations.idiomatic: That year bandits killed the prefects of Dongguan and Langye and used Qushan to guide Wei armies into the region.

sentences.zh: 中大通六年十二月，西南有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year of Zhongdatong, in the southwest there was sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Zhongdatong year 6, thunderlike sounds came from the southwest.

sentences.zh: 其年北梁州刺史蘭欽舉兵反。

translations.literal: That year Beiliang Province Inspector Lan Qin raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That year Beiliang Province Inspector Lan Qin raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 陳太建二年十二月，西北有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Taijian of Chen, in the northwest there was sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Chen's Taijian year 2, thunderlike sounds came from the northwest.

sentences.zh: 其年湘州刺史華皎舉兵反。

translations.literal: That year Xiang Province Inspector Hua Jiao raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xiang Province Inspector Hua Jiao raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 齊天保四年四月，西南有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Tianbao of Qi, in the southwest there was sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Northern Qi's Tianbao year 4, thunderlike sounds came from the southwest.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝不恤天下，興師旅。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor did not care for the realm and raised armies.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor neglected the realm and launched military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 後周建德六年正月，西方有聲如雷。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year of Jiande of Later Zhou, in the west there was sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Northern Zhou's Jiande year 6, thunderlike sounds came from the west.

sentences.zh: 未幾，吐谷渾寇邊。

translations.literal: Before long Tuyuhun raided the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Tuyuhun raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 開皇十四年正月旦，廓州連雲山有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the fourteenth year of Kaihuang, on Lianyun Mountain in Kuozhou there was sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Kaihuang year 14, thunderlike sounds came from Lianyun Mountain in Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 是時五羌反叛，侵擾邊鎮。

translations.literal: At that time the Five Qiang rebelled and harassed the border garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Five Qiang tribes rebelled and harassed the border garrisons.

sentences.zh: 二十年，無雲而雷。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, there was thunder without clouds.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20, thunder sounded though no clouds were present.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「國將易君，下人不靜，小人先命。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'The state will change rulers; the lower people are unsettled; petty men take the lead.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "The state will change rulers; the lower classes are restless; petty men seize the initiative."

sentences.zh: 國凶，有兵甲。

translations.literal: The state is ill-fated; there will be armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The state faces calamity; war will follow.

sentences.zh: 」後數歲，帝崩，漢王諒舉兵反，徙其黨數十萬家。

translations.literal: 'Several years later the emperor died; Prince of Han Liang raised troops in rebellion, and several hundred thousand of his followers were relocated.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the emperor died; Prince Han Liang raised troops in rebellion, and several hundred thousand of his followers were exiled.

sentences.zh: 大業中，滏陽石鼓頻歲鳴。

translations.literal: During Daye, the stone drums of Fuyang sounded year after year.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye era, the stone drums of Fuyang sounded year after year.

sentences.zh: 其後，天下大亂，兵戎並起。

translations.literal: Afterward the realm fell into great disorder and warfare arose everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the realm fell into chaos and warfare erupted everywhere.

sentences.zh: 魚孽梁大同十年三月，帝幸硃方，至四塹中，及玄武湖，魚皆驤首見於上，若望乘輿者。

translations.literal: Fish calamity—in the third month of the tenth year of Datong of Liang, the emperor visited Zhufang; reaching Sichuan and Xuanwu Lake, fish all raised their heads above the water as if looking toward the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Fish calamity: In the third month of Liang's Datong year 10, the emperor visited Zhufang; at Sichuan and Xuanwu Lake, fish raised their heads above the water as if gazing at the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 帝入宮而沒。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the palace and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the palace and drowned.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「魚陰類也，下人象。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Fish are yin kind; they are the image of the lower people.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "Fish belong to yin; they symbolize the common people."

sentences.zh: 又有鱗甲，兵之應也。

translations.literal: Also having scales and armor—the response of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Their scales and armor also foretold warfare.

sentences.zh: 」下人將舉兵圍宮，而䁹睨乘輿之象也。

translations.literal: 'The lower people about to raise troops and besiege the palace—the image of coveting the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: This was the image of the common people rising to besiege the palace and covet the throne.

sentences.zh: 後果有侯景之亂。

translations.literal: Afterward there was indeed the rebellion of Hou Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebellion of Hou Jing followed as predicted.

sentences.zh: 齊後主武平七年，相州鸕鷀泊，魚盡飛去而水涸。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuping of Northern Qi Houzhu, at Cormorant Pool in Xiangzhou, all the fish flew away and the water dried up.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping year 7 of Northern Qi's last emperor, at Cormorant Pool in Xiangzhou, all the fish flew away and the water dried up.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「急之所致。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Caused by haste.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "This comes from haste."

sentences.zh: 魚陰類，下人象也。

translations.literal: Fish are yin kind; they are the image of the lower people.
translations.idiomatic: Fish belong to yin and symbolize the common people.

sentences.zh: 」晏子曰：「河伯以水為國，以魚為百姓。

translations.literal: Master Yan said: 'The River Lord takes water as his state and fish as his common people.'
translations.idiomatic: Master Yan said: "The River Lord takes water as his realm and fish as his people."

sentences.zh: 」水涸魚飛，國亡人散之象。

translations.literal: 'Water drying and fish flying—the image of the state perishing and people scattering.
translations.idiomatic: Water drying up and fish taking flight symbolized the state's destruction and the scattering of its people.

sentences.zh: 明年而國亡。

translations.literal: The next year the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 後周大象元年六月，陽武有鯉魚乘空而鬥。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Daxiang of Later Zhou, at Yangwu carp flew through the air fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Northern Zhou's Daxiang year 1, at Yangwu carp fought in midair.

sentences.zh: 猶臣下興起，小人縱之而鬥也。

translations.literal: Like ministers rising up, petty men inciting them to fight.
translations.idiomatic: It was as if ministers were rising in revolt while petty men incited them to fight.

sentences.zh: 明年帝崩，國失政。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died and the state lost good governance.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor died and the state lost its proper governance.

sentences.zh: 尉迥起兵相州，高祖遣兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: Wei Jiong raised troops at Xiangzhou; Gaozu sent armies and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiong raised troops at Xiangzhou; Gaozu sent armies and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 開皇十七年，大興城西南四里，有袁村，設佛會。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kaihuang, four li southwest of Daxing City there was Yuan Village, where a Buddhist assembly was held.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 17, four li southwest of Daxing City, a Buddhist assembly was held at Yuan Village.

sentences.zh: 有老翁，皓首，白裙襦衣，來食而去。

translations.literal: There was an old man, white-haired, in white skirt and jacket, who came to eat and departed.
translations.idiomatic: An old man with white hair, dressed in white skirt and jacket, came to eat and then departed.

sentences.zh: 眾莫識，追而觀之，行二里許，不復見。

translations.literal: No one recognized him; they pursued and watched; after going about two li he was no longer seen.
translations.idiomatic: No one knew him; people pursued and watched, but after about two li he vanished from sight.

sentences.zh: 但有一陂，中有白魚，長丈餘，小魚從者無數。

translations.literal: There was only a pond with a white fish more than a zhang long, with countless small fish following.
translations.idiomatic: All that remained was a pond containing a white fish more than ten feet long, followed by countless smaller fish.

sentences.zh: 人爭射之，或弓折弦斷。

translations.literal: People competed to shoot it; some bows broke and strings snapped.
translations.idiomatic: People vied to shoot it; some bows broke and bowstrings snapped.

sentences.zh: 後竟中之，剖其腹，得粳飯，始知此魚向老翁也。

translations.literal: Later they finally hit it; cutting open its belly they found polished rice, and then knew this fish was the old man of before.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually they hit it; when they cut open its belly they found steamed rice and realized this fish had been the old man.

sentences.zh: 後數日，漕渠暴溢，射人皆溺死。

translations.literal: Several days later the canal suddenly overflowed, and all who had shot the fish drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the canal burst its banks, and all who had shot the fish drowned.

sentences.zh: 大業十二年，淮陽郡驅人入子城，鑿斷羅郎郭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Daye, Huaiyang Commandery drove people into the inner city to dig through the outer wall of Luolang.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 12, Huaiyang Commandery conscripted laborers to dig through the outer wall of Luolang within the inner city.

sentences.zh: 至女垣之下，有穴，其中得鯉魚，長七尺餘。

translations.literal: Reaching below the parapet, there was a hole; inside they found a carp more than seven chi long.
translations.idiomatic: At the base of the parapet they found a hole containing a carp more than seven feet long.

sentences.zh: 昔魏嘉平四年，魚集武庫屋上。

translations.literal: Formerly in the fourth year of Jiaping of Wei, fish gathered on the roof of the armory.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Jiaoping year 4, fish had gathered on the roof of the armory.

sentences.zh: 王肅以為魚生於水，而亢于屋，水之物失其所也，邊將殆棄甲之變。

translations.literal: Wang Su thought that fish are born in water yet were elevated on a roof—water creatures had lost their place; border generals would likely abandon armor in change.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su reasoned that fish belong in water yet had appeared on a roof—creatures of water displaced from their element; border generals would soon cast off their armor in defeat.

sentences.zh: 後果有東闕之敗。

translations.literal: Afterward there was indeed the defeat at Dongque.
translations.idiomatic: The defeat at Dongque followed as he predicted.

sentences.zh: 是時，長白山賊寇掠河南，月餘，賊至城下。

translations.literal: At that time bandits from Mount Changbai raided Henan; after more than a month the bandits reached below the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits from Mount Changbai raided Henan; after more than a month they reached the city walls.

sentences.zh: 郡兵拒之，反為所敗，男女死者萬余人。

translations.literal: Commandery troops resisted them but were in turn defeated; more than ten thousand men and women died.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery troops resisted but were defeated; more than ten thousand men and women were killed.

sentences.zh: 蟲妖梁大同初，大蝗，籬門松柏葉皆盡。

translations.literal: Insect demon—at the beginning of Datong of Liang, there was a great locust plague; leaves of hedge gates and pine and cypress were all consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Insect omen: At the start of Liang's Datong era, a great locust plague stripped every leaf from hedges, pines, and cypresses.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「介蟲之孽也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Calamity of shelled insects.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "This is a calamity of shelled insects."

sentences.zh: 」與魚同占。

translations.literal: 'Same omen as fish.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as fish calamities.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「食祿不益聖化，天視以蟲。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Eating salary without benefiting sage transformation—Heaven shows insects.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When officials draw salary without advancing sage governance, Heaven sends insects as a sign."

sentences.zh: 蟲無益於人而食萬物也。

translations.literal: Insects benefit people not but eat the myriad things.
translations.idiomatic: Insects benefit no one yet devour all things.

sentences.zh: 」是時公卿皆以虛淡為美，不親職事，無益食物之應也。

translations.literal: 'At that time dukes and ministers all regarded emptiness and detachment as beautiful, did not attend to their duties—the response of eating without benefit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the nobility prized empty detachment over duty—the response to consuming without contributing.

sentences.zh: 後齊天保八年，河北六州、河南十二州蝗。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tianbao of Northern Qi, six prefectures of Hebei and twelve prefectures of Henan had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi's Tianbao year 8, locusts struck six prefectures in Hebei and twelve in Henan.

sentences.zh: 畿人皆祭之。

translations.literal: People of the capital region all made offerings to them.
translations.idiomatic: People throughout the capital region made offerings to the locusts.

sentences.zh: 帝問魏尹丞崔叔瓚曰：「何故蟲？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Wei Yin Assistant Director Cui Shuguan: 'Why insects?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Wei Yin Assistant Director Cui Shuguan: "Why are there insects?"

sentences.zh: 」叔瓚對曰：「《五行志》雲：'土功不時則蝗蟲為災。

translations.literal: 'Shuguan replied: 'The Wuxing Zhi says: "When earthworks are untimely, locusts become a disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: Shuguan replied: "The Treatise on the Five Phases says: 'When earthworks are ill-timed, locusts bring disaster.'"

sentences.zh: '今外築長城，內修三台，故致災也。

translations.literal: 'Now building the Great Wall outside and the Three Terraces inside—therefore this disaster was caused.'
translations.idiomatic: "You are building the Great Wall outside and the Three Terraces inside—that is why this disaster has come."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，毆其頰，擢其發，溷中物塗其頭。

translations.literal: 'The emperor was greatly enraged, struck his cheeks, pulled his hair, and smeared his head with filth from the privy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, struck his cheeks, tore his hair, and smeared his head with filth from the privy.

sentences.zh: 役者不止。

translations.literal: The corvée labor did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: The forced labor continued without pause.

sentences.zh: 九年，山東又蝗，十年，幽州大蝗。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Shandong again had locusts; in the tenth year, Youzhou had a great locust plague.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 locusts returned to Shandong; in year 10 Youzhou suffered a great locust plague.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「刑罰暴虐，食貪不厭，興師動眾，取城修邑，而失眾心，則蟲為災。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When punishments are violent and cruel, eating and greed are insatiable, armies are raised and masses mobilized, cities are taken and towns repaired, and the hearts of the multitude are lost—then insects become a disaster.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "When punishments are savage, greed is insatiable, armies are raised and cities rebuilt at the cost of the people's loyalty—insects become a disaster."

sentences.zh: 」是時帝用刑暴虐，勞役不止之應也。

translations.literal: 'At that time the emperor's use of punishments was violent and cruel, and corvée labor did not stop—the response.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor's punishments were savage and forced labor never ceased—Heaven's response.

sentences.zh: 後周建德二年，關中大蝗。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande of Later Zhou, Guanzhong had a great locust plague.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Zhou's Jiande year 2, Guanzhong suffered a great locust plague.

sentences.zh: 開皇十六年，并州蝗。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaihuang, Bingzhou had locusts.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 16, Bingzhou was struck by locusts.

sentences.zh: 時秦孝王俊裒刻百姓，盛修邸第。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Qin Xiaojun exploited the people and lavishly built mansions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Qin Xiaojun exploited the people and lavishly built mansions.

sentences.zh: 後竟獲譴而死。

translations.literal: Later he was condemned and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually condemned and died.

sentences.zh: 彘禍開皇末，渭南有沙門三人，行頭陀法於人場圃之上。

translations.literal: Pig portent—at the end of Kaihuang, in Weinan three monks practiced dhutanga on people's fields and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Pig omen: At the end of the Kaihuang era, three monks in Weinan practiced ascetic austerities in people's fields and gardens.

sentences.zh: 夜見大豕來詣其所，小豕從者十餘，謂沙門曰：「阿練，我欲得賢聖道，然猶負他一命。

translations.literal: At night they saw a great pig come to their place, with more than ten piglets following, saying to the monks: 'A Lian, I wish to attain the sage and holy Way, yet I still owe one life.'
translations.idiomatic: At night a great pig came to them with more than ten piglets in tow and said to the monks: "Master, I wish to attain the sage's Way, yet I still owe one life."

sentences.zh: 」言罷而去。

translations.literal: 'Having spoken, it departed.
translations.idiomatic: Having spoken, it departed.

sentences.zh: 賢聖道者，君上之所行也。

translations.literal: The sage and holy Way is what the ruler above practices.
translations.idiomatic: The sage's Way is what a ruler should practice.

sentences.zh: 皇太子勇當嗣業，行君上之道，而被囚廢之象也。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Yong should succeed to the enterprise and practice the ruler's Way—the image of being imprisoned and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Yong should have succeeded and ruled—the image of one imprisoned and deposed.

sentences.zh: 一命者，言為煬帝所殺。

translations.literal: One life means he was killed by Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: "One life" meant he would be killed by Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，渭南有人寄宿他舍，夜中聞二豕對語。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang, in Weinan a man lodged at another's house; in the night he heard two pigs conversing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaihuang era, a man lodging in another's house in Weinan heard two pigs conversing in the night.

sentences.zh: 其一曰：「歲將盡，阿耶明日殺我供歲，何處避之？

translations.literal: One said: 'The year is nearly ended; Father will kill me tomorrow for the year's offering—where can I escape?'
translations.idiomatic: One said: "The year is nearly ended; Father will kill me tomorrow for the New Year's feast—where can I hide?"

sentences.zh: 」一答曰：「可向水北姊家。

translations.literal: 'The other answered: 'You can go to elder sister's house north of the river.'
translations.idiomatic: The other answered: "Go to elder sister's house north of the river."

sentences.zh: 」因相隨而去。

translations.literal: 'They then went off together.
translations.idiomatic: They then departed together.

sentences.zh: 天將曉，主人覓豕不得，意是宿客而詰之。

translations.literal: As dawn approached, the host could not find his pig and suspected the lodger, so he questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: As dawn approached, the host could not find his pig and, suspecting the lodger, questioned him.

sentences.zh: 宿客言狀，主人如其言而得豕。

translations.literal: The lodger told what he had heard; the host followed his words and found the pig.
translations.idiomatic: The lodger told what he had heard; the host followed his directions and found the pig.

sentences.zh: 其後蜀王秀得罪，帝將殺之，樂平公主每匡救，得全。

translations.literal: Afterward Prince of Shu Xiu offended and the emperor was about to kill him; Princess of Leping always rescued him and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Shu Xiu fell from favor and the emperor planned to kill him, but Princess of Leping repeatedly intervened and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 後數年而帝崩，歲盡之應。

translations.literal: Several years later the emperor died—the response of the year ending.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the emperor died—the omen of the year's end fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 黑眚黑祥梁承聖三年六月，有黑氣如龍，見於殿內。

translations.literal: Black disaster and black omen—in the sixth month of the third year of Chengsheng of Liang, there was black qi like a dragon seen inside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Black baleful sign: In the sixth month of Liang's Chengsheng year 3, black vapor like a dragon appeared inside the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 近黑祥也。

translations.literal: Close to black omen.
translations.idiomatic: This was a black baleful sign.

sentences.zh: 黑，周所尚之色。

translations.literal: Black is the color Zhou honors.
translations.idiomatic: Black was the color favored by Zhou.

sentences.zh: 今見於殿內，周師入梁之象。

translations.literal: Now seen inside the hall—the image of Zhou armies entering Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Its appearance inside the hall foretold the Zhou armies' conquest of Liang.

sentences.zh: 其年，為周所滅，帝亦遇害。

translations.literal: That year it was destroyed by Zhou; the emperor also met with harm.
translations.idiomatic: That year Liang was destroyed by Zhou, and the emperor was killed.

sentences.zh: 陳太建五年六月，西北有黑雲屬地，散如豬者十餘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Taijian of Chen, in the northwest there was black cloud reaching the ground, scattering like more than ten pigs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Chen's Taijian year 5, black clouds in the northwest reached the ground and scattered like a dozen pigs.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「當有兵起西北。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Warfare will rise in the northwest.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "Warfare will arise in the northwest."

sentences.zh: 」時後周將王軌軍于呂梁。

translations.literal: At that time Later Zhou General Wang Gui was encamped at Luliang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Northern Zhou General Wang Gui was encamped at Luliang.

sentences.zh: 明年，擒吳明徹，軍皆覆沒。

translations.literal: The next year Wu Mingche was captured; the army was entirely destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wu Mingche was captured and his entire army destroyed.

sentences.zh: 火沴水後齊河清元年四月，河、濟清。

translations.literal: Fire harming water—in the fourth month of the first year of Heqing of Northern Qi, the Yellow and Ji Rivers ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: Fire overcoming water: In the fourth month of Northern Qi's Heqing year 1, the Yellow and Ji Rivers ran clear.

sentences.zh: 襄楷曰：「河，諸侯之象。

translations.literal: Xiang Kai said: 'The river is the image of feudal lords.'
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Kai said: "The river symbolizes the feudal lords."

sentences.zh: 應濁反清，諸侯將為天子之象。

translations.literal: Responding from turbid to clear—the image of feudal lords becoming Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The shift from turbid to clear symbolized feudal lords rising to become Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」是後十余歲，隋有天下。

translations.literal: More than ten years later Sui possessed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later Sui conquered the realm.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，武陽郡河清，數裡鏡澈。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, the river at Wuyang Commandery ran clear for several li, mirror-bright.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 3, the river at Wuyang Commandery ran clear for several li, bright as a mirror.

sentences.zh: 十二年，龍門又河清。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, at Longmen the river again ran clear.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, the river at Longmen again ran clear.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，大唐受禪。

translations.literal: Two years later the Great Tang received the abdication.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the Tang received the abdication.

sentences.zh: 陳太建十四年七月，江水赤如血，自建康西至荊州。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourteenth year of Taijian of Chen, the Yangtze ran red as blood from Jiankang west to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Chen's Taijian year 14, the Yangtze ran red as blood from Jiankang west to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 禎明中，江水赤，自方州東至海。

translations.literal: During Zhenming, the Yangtze ran red from Fangzhou east to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenming era, the Yangtze ran red from Fangzhou east to the sea.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「火沴水也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Fire harms water.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "Fire overcomes water."

sentences.zh: 法嚴刑酷，傷水性也。

translations.literal: Harsh laws and cruel punishments harm the nature of water.
translations.idiomatic: Harsh laws and cruel punishments violate the nature of water.

sentences.zh: 五行變節，陰陽相干，氣色繆亂，皆敗亂之象也。

translations.literal: The five phases change their order; yin and yang interfere; qi and color are disordered—all images of defeat and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the five phases shift, yin and yang clash, and colors run awry—all are signs of collapse and disorder.

sentences.zh: 」京房《易占》曰：「水化為血，兵且起。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yizhan says: 'When water turns to blood, warfare will rise.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yizhan says: "When water turns to blood, war will arise."

sentences.zh: 」是時後主初即位，用刑酷暴之應。

translations.literal: At that time Houzhu had newly ascended and used cruel and violent punishments—the response.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the new emperor used cruel and violent punishments—Heaven's response.

sentences.zh: 其後為隋師所滅。

translations.literal: Afterward he was destroyed by Sui armies.
translations.idiomatic: He was later destroyed by Sui armies.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年四月，郢州南浦水，黑如墨。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Zhenming, the waters of Nanpu at Yingzhou were black as ink.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Zhenming year 2, the waters of Nanpu at Yingzhou were black as ink.

sentences.zh: 黑水在關中，而今淮南水黑，荊、揚州之地，陷於關中之應。

translations.literal: Black water is in Guanzhong, yet now the waters of Huainan are black—the response of Jing and Yang falling into Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Black water belongs to Guanzhong, yet now Huainan's waters turned black—foretelling Jing and Yang provinces falling to the north.

sentences.zh: 後周大象元年六月，咸陽池水變為血。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Daxiang of Later Zhou, the pool waters at Xianyang turned to blood.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Northern Zhou's Daxiang year 1, the pool waters at Xianyang turned to blood.

sentences.zh: 與陳太建十四年同占。

translations.literal: Same omen as the fourteenth year of Taijian of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as Chen's Taijian year 14.

sentences.zh: 是時，刑罰嚴急，未幾國亡。

translations.literal: At that time punishments were severe and urgent; before long the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time punishments were severe; before long the state perished.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「思心不容，是謂不聖。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When the mind of reflection does not embrace, this is called not being sage.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "When the mind of reflection fails to embrace all things, it is called lack of wisdom."

sentences.zh: 厥咎瞀，厥罰常風，厥極凶短折。

translations.literal: Its fault is confusion; its punishment is constant wind; its extreme is premature death.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is confusion; the penalty is unrelenting wind; the ultimate consequence is untimely death.

sentences.zh: 有脂夜之妖，有華孽，有牛禍，有心腹之屙，有黃眚黃祥，木金水火沴土。

translations.literal: There are grease-night demons, flower calamities, cow portents, heart-and-belly excrement, yellow disasters and yellow omens; wood, metal, water, and fire harm earth.
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons grease-night demons appear, flower calamities arise, cow omens manifest, heart-and-belly filth appears, and yellow baleful signs emerge—wood, metal, water, and fire all overcome earth.

sentences.zh: 」常風梁天監六年八月戊戌，大風折木。

translations.literal: Constant wind—in the eighth month, wuxu day, of the sixth year of Tianjian of Liang, a great wind snapped trees.
translations.idiomatic: As for "constant wind": on the wuxu day of the eighth month of Liang's Tianjian year 6, a great wind snapped trees.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「角日疾風，天下昏。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'On a jiao day, sudden wind—the realm is darkened.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Sudden wind on a jiao day darkens the realm."

sentences.zh: 不出三月中，兵必起。

translations.literal: Within three months warfare will surely rise.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months war will surely arise.

sentences.zh: 」是歲魏軍入鐘離。

translations.literal: That year Wei armies entered Zhongli.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wei armies entered Zhongli.

sentences.zh: 承聖三年十一月癸未，帝閱武於南城，北風大急，普天昏暗。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, guiwei day, of the third year of Chengsheng, the emperor reviewed troops at the Southern City; the north wind was fierce and the whole sky darkened.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the eleventh month of Chengsheng year 3, the emperor reviewed troops at the Southern City; a fierce north wind darkened the entire sky.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「人君瞀亂之應。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'The response of the ruler's confusion and disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "This is Heaven's response to a ruler's confusion and disorder."

sentences.zh: 」時帝既平侯景，公卿鹹勸帝反丹陽，帝不從，又多猜忌，有瞀亂之行，故天變應之以風。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had pacified Hou Jing; dukes and ministers all urged him to return to Danyang, but the emperor did not follow; he was also much suspicious—having confused and disorderly conduct; therefore Heaven responded with wind.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had pacified Hou Jing, and his ministers urged him to return to Danyang, but he refused; suspicious and confused in his conduct, Heaven answered with wind.

sentences.zh: 是歲為西魏滅。

translations.literal: That year it was destroyed by Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year the state was destroyed by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 陳天嘉六年七月癸未，大風起西南，吹倒靈台候樓。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, guiwei day, of the sixth year of Tiancheng of Chen, a great wind rose from the southwest and blew down the Spirit Terrace observation tower.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiwei day of the seventh month of Chen's Tiancheng year 6, a great wind from the southwest blew down the Spirit Terrace observation tower.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》，以為大臣專恣之咎。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan regards it as the fault of great ministers acting arbitrarily.
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan treats this as the fault of powerful ministers acting arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 時太子沖幼，安成王頊專政，帝不時抑損。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince was young; Prince Ancheng Xu held government power, and the emperor did not restrain him in time.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was young; Prince Ancheng Xu held power, and the emperor failed to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 明年崩，皇太子嗣位，頊遂廢之。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died; the crown prince succeeded, and Xu then deposed him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor died; the crown prince succeeded, and Xu deposed him.

sentences.zh: 太建十二年六月壬戌，大風吹壞皋門中闥。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, renxu day, of the twelfth year of Taijian, a great wind blew down the inner gates of the Gaomen.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day of the sixth month of Taijian year 12, a great wind blew down the inner gates of Gaomen.

sentences.zh: 十二年九月，夜又風，髮屋拔樹。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twelfth year, again at night wind tore off roofs and uprooted trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of that year, wind again tore off roofs and uprooted trees at night.

sentences.zh: 始興王叔陵專恣之應。

translations.literal: The response of Prince Shixing Shuling's arbitrary conduct.
translations.idiomatic: This was the response to Prince Shixing Shuling's arbitrary conduct.

sentences.zh: 至德中，大風吹倒硃雀門。

translations.literal: During Zhide, a great wind blew down the Vermillion Bird Gate.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide era, a great wind blew down the Vermillion Bird Gate.

sentences.zh: 禎明三年六月丁巳，大風，自西北，激濤水入石頭、淮。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, dingsi day, of the third year of Zhenming, a great wind from the northwest drove the surging waters into Shitou and the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day of the sixth month of Zhenming year 3, a great wind from the northwest drove surging waters into Shitou and the Huai.

sentences.zh: 是時，後主任司馬申，誅戮忠諫。

translations.literal: At that time Houzhu employed Sima Shen and executed loyal remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Houzhu employed Sima Shen and executed loyal remonstrators.

sentences.zh: 沈客卿、施文慶專行邪僻。

translations.literal: Shen Keqing and Shi Wenqing practiced wicked ways exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Keqing and Shi Wenqing practiced wicked ways exclusively.

sentences.zh: 江總、孔範等崇長淫縱，杜塞聰明，瞀亂之咎。

translations.literal: Jiang Zong, Kong Fan, and others promoted debauchery, blocked clear hearing—the fault of confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zong, Kong Fan, and others promoted debauchery and blocked wise counsel—the fault of confusion.

sentences.zh: 後齊河清二年，大風，三旬乃止。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heqing of Northern Qi, a great wind lasted thirty days before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi's Heqing year 2, a great wind lasted thirty days before stopping.

sentences.zh: 時帝初委政佞臣和士開，專恣日甚。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor first entrusted government to the flatterer He Shikai, whose arbitrary conduct grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entrusted power to the flatterer He Shikai, whose arbitrary conduct grew daily.

sentences.zh: 天統三年五月，大風，晝晦，髮屋拔樹。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Tiantong, a great wind; day was dark; roofs torn off and trees uprooted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tiantong year 3, a great wind darkened the day and tore off roofs and uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 天變再見，而帝不悟。

translations.literal: Heaven's anomaly appeared again, but the emperor did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning appeared again, but the emperor failed to heed it.

sentences.zh: 明年帝崩。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 後主詔內外表奏，皆先詣士開，然後聞徹。

translations.literal: Houzhu decreed that all memorials inside and outside must first go to Shikai before being forwarded.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu decreed that all memorials must first pass through Shikai before reaching the throne.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王睿、馮翊王潤按士開驕恣，不宜仍居內職，反為士開所譖，睿竟坐死。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhaojun Rui and Prince of Fengyi Run investigated Shikai's arrogance and arbitrary conduct, saying he should not remain in inner office; instead Shikai slandered them, and Rui was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Zhaojun and Fengyi investigated Shikai's arrogance, arguing he should leave inner office; Shikai slandered them, and Prince Zhaojun was executed.

sentences.zh: 士開出入宮掖，生殺在口，尋為琅邪王儼所誅。

translations.literal: Shikai entered and exited the palace women's quarters; life and death were in his mouth; before long he was executed by Prince of Langye Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai moved freely in the inner palace; life and death hung on his word—before long Prince Langye Yan executed him.

sentences.zh: 七年三月，大風起西北，髮屋拔樹。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year, a great wind rose from the northwest, tearing off roofs and uprooting trees.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 7, a great wind from the northwest tore off roofs and uprooted trees.

sentences.zh: 五日乃止。

translations.literal: It stopped after five days.
translations.idiomatic: It stopped after five days.

sentences.zh: 時高阿那瑰、駱提婆等專恣之應。

translations.literal: The response of Gao Anagai, Luo Tiba, and others acting arbitrarily.
translations.idiomatic: This was the response to Gao Anagai, Luo Tiba, and others acting arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 開皇二十年十一月，京都大風，髮屋拔樹，秦、隴壓死者千余人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the twentieth year of Kaihuang, the capital had a great wind that tore off roofs and uprooted trees; in Qin and Long more than a thousand were crushed to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kaihuang year 20, a great wind in the capital tore off roofs and uprooted trees; in Qin and Long more than a thousand were crushed.

sentences.zh: 地大震，鼓皆應。

translations.literal: The earth greatly quaked; all drums responded.
translations.idiomatic: The earth quaked violently; every drum sounded in response.

sentences.zh: 淨刹寺鐘三鳴，佛殿門鎖自開，銅像自出戶外。

translations.literal: The bell at Jingcha Temple rang three times; the Buddha hall door lock opened by itself; the bronze statue walked out the door.
translations.idiomatic: The bell at Jingcha Temple rang three times; the Buddha hall door opened by itself; the bronze statue walked out.

sentences.zh: 鐘鼓自鳴者，近鼓妖也。

translations.literal: Bells and drums sounding by themselves is close to drum demon.
translations.idiomatic: Bells and drums sounding by themselves is akin to the drum-spirit omen.

sentences.zh: 揚雄以為人君不聰，為眾所惑，空名得進，則鼓妖見。

translations.literal: Yang Xiong thought when the ruler is not keen of hearing and is deluded by the multitude, empty names advance—then drum demon appears.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiong held that when a ruler's hearing is dull and he is swayed by the crowd, empty reputations rise—and the drum-spirit omen appears.

sentences.zh: 時獨孤皇后干預政事，左僕射楊素權傾人主。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dugu intervened in government affairs; Left Minister Yang Su's power tilted toward the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu intervened in government; Left Minister Yang Su's power rivaled the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 帝聽二人之讒，而黜僕射高熲，廢太子勇為庶人，晉王釣虛名而見立。

translations.literal: The emperor listened to the slander of these two and dismissed Minister Gao Jiong, deposed Crown Prince Yong as commoner; the Prince of Jin fished for empty reputation and was established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heeded their slander, dismissed Gao Jiong, deposed Crown Prince Yong, and installed the Prince of Jin through empty reputation.

sentences.zh: 思心瞀亂，陰氣盛之象也。

translations.literal: The image of a confused reflective mind and flourishing yin qi.
translations.idiomatic: This was the image of a confused mind and flourishing yin qi.

sentences.zh: 鎖及銅像，並金也。

translations.literal: The lock and bronze statue are both metal.
translations.idiomatic: The lock and bronze statue both represent metal.

sentences.zh: 金動木震之，水沴金之應。

translations.literal: Metal moved by wood's quaking—the response of water harming metal.
translations.idiomatic: Metal shaken by wood's quaking—the response of water overcoming metal.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「失眾心甚之所致也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Caused by losing the hearts of the multitude to an extreme degree.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary on the Great Plan says: "This comes from losing the people's hearts utterly."

sentences.zh: 」高熲、楊勇無罪而鹹廢黜，失眾心也。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong and Yang Yong were innocent yet both deposed—losing the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and Yang Yong were innocent yet both deposed—losing the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年，西河有胡人，乘騾在道，忽為回風所飄，並一車上千餘尺，乃墜，皆碎焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Renshou, in Xihe there was a Hu man riding a mule on the road; suddenly a whirlwind blew him and a cart more than a thousand chi into the air, then they fell and were shattered.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou year 2, in Xihe a Hu man riding a mule was suddenly blown by a whirlwind, cart and all, more than a thousand feet into the air, then shattered on falling.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「眾逆同志，至德乃潛，厥異風。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yizhuan says: 'When the multitude rebels together, supreme virtue is hidden; its anomaly is wind.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the multitude rebels together and supreme virtue is hidden, the anomaly is wind."

sentences.zh: 」後二載，漢王諒在并州，潛謀逆亂，車及騾騎之象也。

translations.literal: Two years later Prince of Han Liang was at Bingzhou, secretly plotting rebellion—the image of carts and mule cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Prince Han Liang at Bingzhou secretly plotted rebellion—the image of carts and cavalry.

sentences.zh: 升空而墜，顛隕之應也。

translations.literal: Rising into the air and falling—the response of toppling ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Rising into the air and falling foretold toppling ruin.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，無妄動車騎，終當覆敗，而諒不悟。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: do not rashly move chariots and cavalry—you will ultimately be overturned and defeated; yet Liang did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: do not rashly mobilize chariots and cavalry—you will be overturned; yet Liang failed to heed it.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，諒發兵反，州縣響應，眾至數十萬。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Liang raised troops in rebellion; commanderies and counties responded; the multitude reached several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu died, Liang raised troops; commanderies responded; his forces reached hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 月餘而敗。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 夜妖梁承聖二年十月丁卯，大風，晝晦，天地昏暗。

translations.literal: Night demon—in the tenth month, dingmao day, of the second year of Chengsheng of Liang, a great wind; day was dark; heaven and earth were dim.
translations.idiomatic: Night demon: On the dingmao day of the tenth month of Liang's Chengsheng year 2, a great wind darkened the day and dimmed heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 近夜妖也。

translations.literal: Close to night demon.
translations.idiomatic: This was a night-demon omen.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「羽日風，天下昏，人大疾。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'On a yu day, wind—the realm is darkened; people have great illness.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Wind on a yu day darkens the realm; the people suffer great illness."

sentences.zh: 不然，多寇盜。

translations.literal: Otherwise, many bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, bandits and robbers multiply.

sentences.zh: 」三年為西魏所滅。

translations.literal: Three years later it was destroyed by Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later the state was destroyed by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 陳禎明三年正月朔旦，雲霧晦冥，入鼻辛酸。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the third year of Zhenming of Chen, clouds and mist were dim; entering the nose was sour and bitter.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of Chen's Zhenming year 3, clouds and mist were dim; the air in one's nostrils was sour and bitter.

sentences.zh: 後主昏昧，近夜妖也。

translations.literal: Houzhu was benighted—close to night demon.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu was benighted—this was a night-demon omen.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「王失中，臣下強盛，以蔽君明，則雲陰。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When the king loses the center, ministers below are strong and flourishing, obscuring the ruler's clarity—then clouds are yin.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "When the king loses the center and powerful ministers obscure his clarity, yin clouds appear."

sentences.zh: 」是時北軍臨江，柳莊、任蠻奴並進中款，後主惑佞臣孔範之言，而昏暗不能用，以至覆敗。

translations.literal: At that time northern armies were on the Yangtze; Liu Zhuang and Ren Manu both offered loyal counsel, but Houzhu was deluded by the flatterer Kong Fan and was benighted and unable to use them, leading to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Northern armies stood on the Yangtze; Liu Zhuang and Ren Manu offered loyal counsel, but Houzhu, deluded by Kong Fan, could not act—and fell.

sentences.zh: 東魏武定四年冬，大霧六日，晝夜不解。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Wuding of Eastern Wei, great fog lasted six days; day and night did not clear.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Eastern Wei's Wuding year 4, great fog lasted six days without clearing.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「晝而晦冥若夜者，陰侵陽，臣將侵君之象也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When day is dim as night, yin invades yang—the image of ministers about to invade the ruler.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "When day is dim as night, yin invades yang—ministers will invade the ruler."

sentences.zh: 」明年，元瑾、劉思逸謀殺大將軍之應。

translations.literal: The next year, Yuan Jin and Liu Siyi plotted to kill the great general—the response.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yuan Jin and Liu Siyi plotted to kill the great general—the omen fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 周大象二年，尉迥敗於相州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daxiang of Later Zhou, Wei Jiong was defeated at Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Zhou's Daxiang year 2, Wei Jiong was defeated at Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 坑其党與數萬人于遊豫園。

translations.literal: His followers numbering tens of thousands were buried in a pit at Youyu Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of his followers were buried in a pit at Youyu Garden.

sentences.zh: 其處每聞鬼夜哭聲。

translations.literal: At that place one often heard ghosts crying at night.
translations.idiomatic: At that place ghosts were often heard crying at night.

sentences.zh: 范洪《五行傳》曰：「哭者死亡之表，近夜妖也。

translations.literal: Fan Hong's Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Crying is the manifestation of death; close to night demon.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan Hong's Wuxing Commentary says: "Crying manifests death—it is a night-demon omen."

sentences.zh: 鬼而夜哭者，將有死亡之應。

translations.literal: Ghosts crying at night will have the response of death.
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts crying at night foretell death.

sentences.zh: 」京房《易飛候》曰：「鬼夜哭，國將亡。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Ghosts crying at night—the state will perish.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Ghosts crying at night—the state will perish."

sentences.zh: 」明年，周氏王公皆見殺，周室亦亡。

translations.literal: The next year Zhou princes were all killed; the Zhou house also perished.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhou princes were all killed and the Zhou dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，仁壽宮及長城之下，數聞鬼哭。

translations.literal: During Renshou, below Renshou Palace and the Great Wall, ghost crying was often heard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era, ghostly crying was often heard below Renshou Palace and the Great Wall.
