sentences.zh: 尋而獻後及帝，相次而崩于仁壽宮。

translations.literal: Before long Empress Xian and the emperor successively died at Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Empress Xian and the emperor died in succession at Renshou Palace.

sentences.zh: 大業八年，楊玄感作亂於東都。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daye, Yang Xuangan raised rebellion at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 8, Yang Xuangan raised rebellion at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 尚書樊子蓋坑其党與于長夏門外，前後數萬。

translations.literal: Minister Fan Zigai buried his followers in a pit outside Changxia Gate—altogether tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Fan Zigai buried his followers in a pit outside Changxia Gate—tens of thousands in all.

sentences.zh: 洎于末年，數聞其處鬼哭，有呻吟之聲。

translations.literal: By the end of the era, ghost crying was often heard at that place, with groaning sounds.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the era, ghostly crying and groaning were often heard there.

sentences.zh: 與前同占。

translations.literal: Same omen as before.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as before.

sentences.zh: 其後王世充害越王侗於洛陽。

translations.literal: Afterward Wang Shichong killed Prince of Yue Tong at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Wang Shichong killed Prince Yue Tong at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 華孽後齊武平元年，槐華而不結實。

translations.literal: Flower calamity—in the first year of Wuping of Northern Qi, locust trees bloomed but bore no fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Flower calamity: In Northern Qi's Wuping year 1, locust trees bloomed but bore no fruit.

sentences.zh: 槐，三公之位也，華而不實，萎落之象。

translations.literal: The locust tree is the position of the Three Dukes; blooming without fruit is the image of withering and falling.
translations.idiomatic: The locust tree symbolizes the Three Dukes; blooming without fruit foretold their withering and fall.

sentences.zh: 至明年，錄尚書事和士開伏誅。

translations.literal: By the next year, Chief Minister He Shikai was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chief Minister He Shikai was executed.

sentences.zh: 隴東王胡長仁，太保、琅邪王儼皆遇害。

translations.literal: Prince of Longdong Hu Changren, Grand Tutor Prince of Langye Yan—all met with harm.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Longdong Hu Changren and Grand Tutor Prince Langye Yan were all killed.

sentences.zh: 左丞相段韶薨。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Duan Shao died.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Duan Shao died.

sentences.zh: 陳後主時，有張貴妃、孔貴嬪，並有國色，稱為妖豔。

translations.literal: During Chen Houzhu's reign there were Consort Zhang and Consort Kong, both of national beauty, called bewitchingly lovely.
translations.idiomatic: During Houzhu's reign Consorts Zhang and Kong, both renowned for beauty, were called bewitchingly lovely.

sentences.zh: 後主惑之，寵冠宮掖，每充侍從，詩酒為娛。

translations.literal: Houzhu was deluded by them; their favor topped the palace; they always attended him; poetry and wine were their pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu was captivated; they held supreme favor in the palace, always at his side, devoted to poetry and wine.

sentences.zh: 一入後庭，數旬不出，荒淫侈靡，莫知紀極。

translations.literal: Once entering the rear palace, for several ten-day periods they did not emerge; debauchery and extravagance beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Once they entered the inner palace, they did not emerge for weeks; debauchery and extravagance knew no bounds.

sentences.zh: 府庫空竭，頭會箕斂，天下怨叛，將士離心。

translations.literal: Treasury emptied; taxes piled high; the realm rebelled; officers and soldiers lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury emptied; taxes piled high; the realm rebelled; officers and soldiers lost heart.

sentences.zh: 敵人鼓行而進，莫有死戰之士。

translations.literal: The enemy marched in formation; none would fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy marched in formation; none would fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 女德之咎也。

translations.literal: The fault of female virtue.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fault of female influence.

sentences.zh: 及敗亡之際，後主與此姬俱投于井，隋師執張貴妃而戮之，以謝江東。

translations.literal: At the moment of defeat and ruin, Houzhu and these consorts together threw themselves into a well; Sui armies seized Consort Zhang and executed her to appease Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of defeat, Houzhu and these consorts threw themselves into a well; Sui forces seized Consort Zhang and executed her to appease Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「華者，猶榮華容色之象也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Flower is the image of splendor and countenance.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Flower symbolizes splendor and beauty."

sentences.zh: 以色亂國，故謂華孽。

translations.literal: Using beauty to disorder the state—therefore called flower calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Using beauty to disorder the state—this is called flower calamity.

sentences.zh: 齊後主有寵姬馮小憐，慧而有色，能彈琵琶，尤工歌儛。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Houzhu had a favored consort Feng Xiaolian, clever and beautiful, able to play the pipa, especially skilled in song and dance.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's last emperor had a favored consort Feng Xiaolian—clever and beautiful, skilled on the pipa and especially in song and dance.

sentences.zh: 後主惑之，拜為淑妃。

translations.literal: Houzhu was deluded by her and made her Shufei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was captivated and made her Shufei.

sentences.zh: 選彩女數千，為之羽從，一女之飾，動費千金。

translations.literal: Several thousand colored women were selected as her retinue; one woman's adornment cost a thousand gold.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand attendants were selected for her retinue; a single woman's adornments cost a thousand gold pieces.

sentences.zh: 帝從禽於三堆，而周師大至，邊吏告急，相望於道。

translations.literal: The emperor was hunting at Sandui when Zhou armies arrived in force; border officials reported urgent news one after another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was hunting at Sandui when Zhou armies arrived; urgent reports lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 帝欲班師，小憐意不已，更請合圍。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to withdraw the army; Xiaolian was unwilling and asked to continue the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to withdraw, but Xiaolian insisted on continuing the hunt.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed her.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor complied.

sentences.zh: 由是遲留，而晉州遂陷。

translations.literal: Because of this delay, Jinzhou then fell.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this delay, Jinzhou fell.

sentences.zh: 後與周師相遇于晉州之下，坐小憐而失機者數矣，因而國滅。

translations.literal: Later meeting Zhou armies below Jinzhou, because of Xiaolian he lost opportunity several times, and thus the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Later, meeting Zhou armies below Jinzhou, he lost opportunity repeatedly because of Xiaolian—and the state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 齊之士庶，至今咎之。

translations.literal: The gentry and common people of Qi blame her to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Qi gentry and commoners blame her to this day.

sentences.zh: 牛禍梁武陵王紀祭城隍神，將烹牛，忽有赤蛇繞牛口，牛禍也。

translations.literal: Cow portent—Prince of Wuling Ji of Liang was sacrificing to the city god; about to cook an ox, suddenly a red snake coiled around the ox's mouth—cow portent.
translations.idiomatic: Cow omen: Prince Wuling Xiao Ji was sacrificing to the city god; as an ox was about to be cooked, a red snake coiled around its mouth.

sentences.zh: 象類言之，又為龍蛇之孽。

translations.literal: Speaking in terms of elephant categories, it is also dragon-and-snake calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In symbolic terms, it was also a dragon-and-snake calamity.

sentences.zh: 魯宣公三年，郊牛之口傷，時以為天不享。

translations.literal: In the third year of Duke Xuan of Lu, the suburban ox's mouth was injured; at the time it was thought Heaven did not accept the offering.
translations.idiomatic: In Lu Duke Xuan's year 3, the suburban ox's mouth was injured; at the time Heaven was thought to reject the offering.

sentences.zh: 棄宣公也。

translations.literal: Duke Xuan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Xuan was abandoned by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 《五行傳》曰：「逆君道傷，故有龍蛇之孽。

translations.literal: The Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When the ruler's way is violated and injured, therefore there are dragon-and-snake calamities.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "When the ruler's way is violated, dragon-and-snake calamities arise."

sentences.zh: 」是時紀雖以赴援為名，而實妄自尊亢。

translations.literal: At that time Ji, though nominally going to aid, in fact arrogantly exalted himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though nominally going to aid, Ji in fact arrogantly exalted himself.

sentences.zh: 思心之咎，神不享，君道傷之應。

translations.literal: The fault of the reflective mind; the spirits do not accept; the response of the ruler's way being injured.
translations.idiomatic: The fault of a confused mind; the spirits rejected him—the ruler's way was injured.

sentences.zh: 果為元帝所敗。

translations.literal: In the end he was defeated by Emperor Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was ultimately defeated by Emperor Yuan.

sentences.zh: 後齊武平二年，并州獻五足牛，牛禍也。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuping of Northern Qi, Bingzhou presented a five-footed ox—cow portent.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi's Wuping year 2, Bingzhou presented a five-footed ox—a cow omen.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「牛事應，宮室之象也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Cow affairs respond—the image of palace halls.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Cow omens respond to palace affairs—the image of palace halls."

sentences.zh: 」帝尋大發卒，于仙都苑穿池築山，樓殿間起，窮華極麗。

translations.literal: The emperor soon massively mobilized troops, digging pools and building mountains in the Xiandu Garden, towers and halls rising one after another, extreme splendor and beauty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon conscripted masses of laborers, digging pools and building mountains in the Xiandu Garden, towers and halls of extreme splendor rising one after another.

sentences.zh: 功始就而亡國。

translations.literal: When the work was just completed the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was just completed, the state perished.

sentences.zh: 後周建德六年，陽武有獸三，狀如水牛，一黃，一赤，一黑。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the sixth year of Jiande of Later Zhou, at Yangwu there were three beasts shaped like water buffalo—one yellow, one red, one black.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Northern Zhou's Jiande year 6, at Yangwu three beasts shaped like water buffalo appeared—one yellow, one red, one black.

sentences.zh: 與黑者鬥久之，黃者自傍觸之，黑者死，黃亦俱入於河。

translations.literal: Fighting with the black one for a long time, the yellow one from the side struck it; the black one died; the yellow also together entered the river.
translations.idiomatic: The red fought the black for a long time; the yellow struck from the side; the black died; the yellow also entered the river.

sentences.zh: 近牛禍也。

translations.literal: Close to cow portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a cow omen.

sentences.zh: 黑者，周之所尚色。

translations.literal: The black one is the color Zhou honors.
translations.idiomatic: Black was the color Zhou favored.

sentences.zh: 死者，滅亡之象。

translations.literal: The dead one is the image of destruction and perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Death symbolized destruction.

sentences.zh: 後數載，周果滅而隋有天下，旗牲尚赤，戎服以黃。

translations.literal: Several years later Zhou indeed perished and Sui possessed the realm; banners and sacrificial animals honored red; military dress used yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Zhou fell and Sui conquered the realm—banners and sacrifices honored red, military dress used yellow.

sentences.zh: 大業初，恆山有牛，四腳膝上各生一蹄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, at Hengshan there was an ox with a hoof growing on each knee of its four legs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Daye, at Hengshan an ox grew a hoof on each of its four knees.

sentences.zh: 其後建東都，築長城，開溝洫。

translations.literal: Afterward the Eastern Capital was built, the Great Wall constructed, and canals dug.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Eastern Capital was built, the Great Wall constructed, and canals dug.

sentences.zh: 心腹之屙陳禎明三年，隋師臨江，後主從容而言曰：「齊兵三來，周師再來，無弗摧敗。

translations.literal: Heart-and-belly excrement—in the third year of Zhenming of Chen, Sui armies were on the Yangtze; Houzhu calmly said: 'Qi armies came three times, Zhou armies twice—all were utterly defeated.'
translations.idiomatic: Heart-and-belly filth: In Chen's Zhenming year 3, as Sui armies reached the Yangtze, Houzhu said calmly: "Qi came three times, Zhou twice—all were crushed."

sentences.zh: 彼何為者？

translations.literal: What are they doing?
translations.idiomatic: What are they doing?

sentences.zh: 」都官尚書孔范曰：「長江天塹，古以為限隔南北。

translations.literal: Minister of Palace Affairs Kong Fan said: 'The Yangtze is Heaven's moat, anciently regarded as the barrier between north and south.'
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Palace Affairs Kong Fan said: "The Yangtze is Heaven's moat, the ancient barrier between north and south."

sentences.zh: 今日北軍豈能飛渡耶？

translations.literal: Today can the northern armies fly across?
translations.idiomatic: Can the northern armies fly across today?

sentences.zh: 臣每患官卑，彼若渡來，臣為太尉矣。

translations.literal: I always worry my rank is low; if they cross, I shall be Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: I always worry my rank is too low; if they cross, I shall become Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 」後主大悅，因奏妓縱酒，賦詩不輟。

translations.literal: Houzhu was greatly pleased and therefore had music performed, drank freely, and composed poetry without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu was delighted, summoned musicians, drank freely, and composed poetry without cease.

sentences.zh: 心腹之屙也。

translations.literal: Heart-and-belly excrement.
translations.idiomatic: This was heart-and-belly filth.

sentences.zh: 存亡之機，定之俄頃，君臣旰食不暇，後主已不知懼，孔範從而蕩之，天奪其心，曷能不敗？

translations.literal: The moment of survival or ruin is decided in an instant; ruler and ministers should have no time even to eat at dusk; Houzhu already did not know fear; Kong Fan further led him astray; Heaven took his heart—how could he not be defeated?
translations.idiomatic: Survival or ruin is decided in an instant; yet Houzhu felt no fear while Kong Fan led him astray—Heaven had taken his heart; how could he not fall?

sentences.zh: 陳國遂亡，範亦遠徙。

translations.literal: The state of Chen then perished; Fan was also exiled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Chen fell; Fan was exiled.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣帝嘗宴於東山，投杯赫怒，下詔西伐，極陳甲兵之盛。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Emperor Wenxuan once feasted at Mount Dong; he threw his cup in rage, issued an edict for a western campaign, and fully displayed the strength of armor and troops.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Emperor Wenxuan once feasted at Mount Dong, threw his cup in rage, and issued an edict for a western campaign displaying the full strength of his armies.

sentences.zh: 既而泣謂群臣曰：「黑衣非我所制。

translations.literal: Then weeping he told the assembled ministers: 'Black robes are not what I control.'
translations.idiomatic: Then weeping he told his ministers: "Black robes are not mine to command."

sentences.zh: 」卒不行。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not go.

sentences.zh: 有識者以帝精魄已亂，知帝祚之不永。

translations.literal: Those with insight, seeing the emperor's spirit already disordered, knew the imperial fortune would not be long.
translations.idiomatic: Those with insight, seeing the emperor's spirit disordered, knew his reign would not be long.

sentences.zh: 帝后竟得心疾，耽荒酒色，性忽狂暴，數年而崩。

translations.literal: The emperor afterward indeed got heart disease, indulged in wine and sex, suddenly became violent and wild, and died within several years.
translations.idiomatic: He afterward developed heart disease, indulged in wine and sex, turned violent, and died within years.

sentences.zh: 武成帝丁太后憂，緋袍如故。

translations.literal: Emperor Wucheng during Empress Dowager Ding's mourning still wore crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng during Empress Dowager Ding's mourning still wore crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 未幾，登三台，置酒作樂，侍者進白袍，帝大怒，投之台下。

translations.literal: Before long he ascended the Three Terraces, set out wine and made music; attendants presented white robes; the emperor was greatly enraged and threw them below the terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he ascended the Three Terraces for wine and music; when attendants presented white mourning robes, he flew into a rage and threw them off the terrace.

sentences.zh: 未幾而崩。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 黃眚黃祥梁大同元年，天雨土。

translations.literal: Yellow disaster and yellow omen—in the first year of Datong of Liang, heaven rained earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow baleful sign: In Liang's Datong year 1, earth rained from heaven.

sentences.zh: 二年，天雨灰，其色黃。

translations.literal: In the second year, heaven rained ash, yellow in color.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, ash rained from heaven, yellow in color.

sentences.zh: 近黃祥也。

translations.literal: Close to yellow omen.
translations.idiomatic: This was a yellow baleful sign.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「聞善不及，茲謂有知。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Hearing good but not reaching it—this is called having knowledge.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Hearing of good but failing to attain it—this is called having knowledge without acting."

sentences.zh: 厥異黃，厥咎龍，厥災不嗣。

translations.literal: Its anomaly is yellow; its fault is dragon; its disaster is no succession.
translations.idiomatic: The anomaly is yellow; the fault is dragon; the disaster is no succession.

sentences.zh: 蔽賢絕道之咎也。

translations.literal: The fault of obscuring the worthy and cutting off the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The fault of obscuring the worthy and cutting off the Way.

sentences.zh: 」時帝自以為聰明博達，惡人勝己。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor considered himself intelligent and broadly learned, hating those who surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor considered himself brilliant and hated those who surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 又篤信佛法，捨身為奴，絕道蔽賢之罰也。

translations.literal: Also deeply believing in Buddhism, offering his body as a slave—the punishment of cutting off the Way and obscuring the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He also devoted himself to Buddhism, offering his body as a slave—the penalty for cutting off the Way and obscuring the worthy.

sentences.zh: 大寶元年正月，天雨黃沙。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dabao, heaven rained yellow sand.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dabao year 1, yellow sand rained from heaven.

sentences.zh: 二年，簡文帝夢丸土而吞之。

translations.literal: In the second year, Emperor Jianwen dreamed of swallowing a ball of earth.
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, Emperor Jianwen dreamed of swallowing a ball of earth.

sentences.zh: 尋為侯景所廢，以土囊壓之而斃，諸子遇害，不嗣之應也。

translations.literal: Before long he was deposed by Hou Jing, suffocated with an earth bag and died; his sons met with harm—the response of no succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hou Jing deposed him, suffocated him with an earth bag, and killed his sons—the omen of no succession fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 陳後主時，夢黃衣人圍城。

translations.literal: During Chen Houzhu's reign, he dreamed of men in yellow clothing surrounding the city.
translations.idiomatic: During Houzhu's reign, he dreamed of men in yellow clothing surrounding the city.

sentences.zh: 後主惡之，繞城橘樹，盡伐去之。

translations.literal: Houzhu hated it and had the orange trees around the city wall all cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu hated the dream and had all the orange trees around the city wall cut down.

sentences.zh: 隋高祖受禪之後，上下通服黃衣。

translations.literal: After Sui Gaozu received the abdication, above and below all wore yellow clothing.
translations.idiomatic: After Sui Gaozu received the abdication, everyone wore yellow clothing.

sentences.zh: 未幾隋師攻圍之應也。

translations.literal: Before long the response of Sui armies attacking and besieging.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sui armies besieged the city—the omen fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 後周大象二年正月，天雨黃土，移時乃息。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Daxiang of Later Zhou, heaven rained yellow earth; after a while it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Northern Zhou's Daxiang year 2, yellow earth rained from heaven, then stopped.

sentences.zh: 與大同元年同占。

translations.literal: Same omen as the first year of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as Datong year 1.

sentences.zh: 時帝昏狂滋甚，期年而崩，至於靜帝，用遜厥位。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's madness grew worse; within a year he died; as for Emperor Jing, he was forced to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's madness worsened; within a year he died; Emperor Jing was forced to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 絕道不嗣之應也。

translations.literal: The response of cutting off the Way and no succession.
translations.idiomatic: The response of cutting off the Way and no succession.

sentences.zh: 開皇二年，京師雨土。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaihuang, the capital rained earth.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 2, earth rained on the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時帝懲周室諸侯微弱，以亡天下，故分封諸子，並為行台，專制方面。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor, learning from Zhou's weak feudal lords losing the realm, therefore enfeoffed his sons, all as mobile administrations, monopolizing their regions.
translations.idiomatic: Learning from Zhou's weak feudal lords, the emperor enfeoffed his sons as regional governors with full autonomy.

sentences.zh: 失土之故，有土氣之祥，其後諸王各謀為逆亂。

translations.literal: The reason for losing earth—there was an earth-qi omen; afterward the princes each plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Losing earth brought an earth-qi omen; afterward the princes each plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「天雨土，百姓勞苦而無功。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Heaven rains earth—the common people toil without achievement.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When heaven rains earth, the people toil without achievement."

sentences.zh: 」其時營都邑。

translations.literal: At that time the capital city was being built.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the capital was being built.

sentences.zh: 後起仁壽宮，頹山堙谷，丁匠死者太半。

translations.literal: Afterward Renshou Palace was raised; mountains were demolished and valleys filled; more than half the laborers died.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Renshou Palace was built; mountains were demolished and valleys filled; more than half the laborers died.

sentences.zh: 裸蟲之孽梁太清元年，丹陽有莫氏妻，生男，眼在頂上，大如兩歲兒。

translations.literal: Naked insect calamity—in the first year of Taiqing of Liang, in Danyang a Mrs. Mo bore a boy with eyes on the crown of his head, as large as a two-year-old child.
translations.idiomatic: Naked-insect calamity: In Liang's Taiqing year 1, in Danyang Mrs. Mo bore a boy with eyes on the crown of his head, as large as a two-year-old's.

sentences.zh: 墜地而言曰：「兒是旱疫鬼，不得住。

translations.literal: Falling to the ground he spoke: 'I am the drought-plague ghost; I cannot stay.'
translations.idiomatic: Falling to the ground he spoke: "I am the drought-plague ghost; I cannot stay."

sentences.zh: 」母曰：「汝當令我得過。

translations.literal: The mother said: 'You should let me pass.'
translations.idiomatic: The mother said: "You should let me pass."

sentences.zh: 」疫鬼曰：「有上官，何得自由。

translations.literal: The plague ghost said: 'There is a superior official; how can I be free.'
translations.idiomatic: The plague ghost said: "There is a superior official; I cannot act freely."

sentences.zh: 母可急作絳帽，故當無憂。

translations.literal: Mother can quickly make a crimson hat; then you should have no worry.
translations.idiomatic: Make a crimson hat quickly and you will have no worry.

sentences.zh: 」母不暇作帽，以絳系發。

translations.literal: The mother had no time to make a hat and tied crimson to her hair.
translations.idiomatic: The mother had no time to make a hat and tied crimson cloth in her hair.

sentences.zh: 自是旱疫者二年，揚、徐、兗、豫尤甚。

translations.literal: From this drought and plague lasted two years; Yang, Xu, Yan, and Yu were especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: From this drought and plague lasted two years; Yang, Xu, Yan, and Yu were especially hard hit.

sentences.zh: 莫氏鄉鄰，多以絳免，他土效之無驗。

translations.literal: Mo's neighbors mostly escaped with crimson; other places imitating it had no effect.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's neighbors mostly escaped with crimson; others who imitated it found no effect.

sentences.zh: 大寶二年，京口人于藏兒，年五歲，登城西南角大樓，打鼓作《長江櫑》。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dabao, Yu Zang'er of Jingkou, five years old, climbed the great tower at the southwest corner of the city wall, beat a drum and performed The Yangtze River Lei.
translations.idiomatic: In Dabao year 2, five-year-old Yu Zang'er of Jingkou climbed the great tower at the city's southwest corner, beat a drum, and performed The Yangtze River Lei.

sentences.zh: 鼓，兵象也。

translations.literal: The drum is the image of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The drum symbolizes warfare.

sentences.zh: 是時侯景亂江南。

translations.literal: At that time Hou Jing disturbed Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hou Jing ravaged Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 陳永定三年，有人長三丈，見羅浮山，通身潔白，衣服楚麗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongding of Chen, there was a man three zhang tall seen at Mount Luofu, entirely white, in splendid Chu dress.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen's Yongding year 3, a man three zhang tall was seen at Mount Luofu, entirely white, in splendid Chu dress.

sentences.zh: 京房占曰：「長人見，亡。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's divination says: 'When a tall man appears—perish.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's divination says: "When a tall man appears—the state will perish."

sentences.zh: 」後二歲，帝崩。

translations.literal: Two years later the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 後主為太子時，有婦人突入東宮而大言曰：「畢國主。

translations.literal: When Houzhu was crown prince, a woman suddenly entered the Eastern Palace and cried out: 'The state-lord is finished.'
translations.idiomatic: When Houzhu was crown prince, a woman burst into the Eastern Palace crying: "The state-lord is finished."

sentences.zh: 」後主立而祚終之應也。

translations.literal: The response of Houzhu ascending and the fortune ending.
translations.idiomatic: The omen of Houzhu ascending and his reign ending.

sentences.zh: 至德三年八月，建康人家婢死，埋之九日而更生。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Zhide, a maid of a Jiankang household died, was buried, and after nine days revived.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Zhide year 3, a Jiankang maid died, was buried, and revived after nine days.

sentences.zh: 有牧牛人聞而出之。

translations.literal: A cattle herder heard and dug her out.
translations.idiomatic: A cattle herder heard and dug her out.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年，有船下，忽聞人言曰：「明年亂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenming, on a boat someone suddenly heard a voice say: 'Next year there will be disorder.'
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 2, on a boat someone heard a voice say: "Next year there will be disorder."

sentences.zh: 」視之，得死嬰兒，長二尺而無頭。

translations.literal: Looking, they found a dead infant two chi long without a head.
translations.idiomatic: Looking, they found a headless dead infant two chi long.

sentences.zh: 明年陳滅。

translations.literal: The next year Chen perished.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chen fell.

sentences.zh: 齊天保中，臨漳有婦人產子，二頭共體。

translations.literal: During Tianbao of Qi, in Linzhang a woman bore a child with two heads sharing one body.
translations.idiomatic: During Northern Qi's Tianbao era, in Linzhang a woman bore a child with two heads sharing one body.

sentences.zh: 是後政由奸佞，上下無別，兩頭之應也。

translations.literal: Afterward government was in the hands of wicked flatterers; above and below were undifferentiated—the response of two heads.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward wicked flatterers held power; above and below were undifferentiated—the omen of two heads fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 後主時，有桑門，貌若狂人，見烏則向之作禮，見沙門則毆辱之。

translations.literal: During Houzhu's reign there was a monk who seemed mad; seeing crows he bowed to them; seeing monks he beat and insulted them.
translations.idiomatic: During Houzhu's reign a seemingly mad monk bowed to crows but beat and insulted monks.

sentences.zh: 烏，周色也。

translations.literal: The crow is Zhou's color.
translations.idiomatic: The crow was Zhou's color.

sentences.zh: 未幾，齊為周所吞，滅除佛法。

translations.literal: Before long Qi was swallowed by Zhou and Buddhism was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qi was swallowed by Zhou and Buddhism was abolished.

sentences.zh: 後周保定三年，有人產子男，陰在背上如尾，兩足指如獸爪。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoqing of Later Zhou, a man bore a male child with genitals on his back like a tail; two foot toes like beast claws.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Zhou's Baoqing year 3, a man bore a son with genitals on his back like a tail and foot toes like beast claws.

sentences.zh: 陰不當生於背而生於背者，陰陽反覆，君臣顛倒之象。

translations.literal: Genitals should not be born on the back; born on the back—the image of yin and yang reversed and ruler and minister inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Genitals should not appear on the back—this symbolized yin and yang reversed and ruler and minister inverted.

sentences.zh: 人足不當有爪而有爪者，將致攫人之變也。

translations.literal: Human feet should not have claws; having claws—about to bring the change of seizing people.
translations.idiomatic: Human feet should not have claws—this foretold violent seizure of people.

sentences.zh: 是時，晉蕩公宇文護專擅朝政，征伐自己，陰懷篡逆。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Jindang Yuwen Hu monopolized court government; campaigns were his own; secretly harboring usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duke Jindang Yuwen Hu monopolized government, commanded campaigns himself, and secretly plotted usurpation.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，君臣之分已倒矣，將行攫噬之禍。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the distinction of ruler and minister is already inverted; the calamity of seizing and devouring will be enacted.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: ruler and minister are inverted; seizing and devouring will follow.

sentences.zh: 帝見變而悟，遂誅晉公，親萬機，躬節儉，克平齊國，號為高祖。

translations.literal: The emperor saw the anomaly and understood; then executed the Duke of Jin, personally handled the myriad affairs, practiced frugality himself, conquered Qi, and was called Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the omen and acted; he executed Yuwen Hu, took personal control, practiced frugality, conquered Qi, and became known as Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 轉禍為福之效也。

translations.literal: The effect of turning calamity into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The effect of turning calamity into blessing.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，有強練者，佯狂，持一瓠，至晉蕩公護門而擊破之，曰：「身尚可，子苦矣。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wu's reign there was Qiang Lian who feigned madness; holding a gourd he came to Duke of Jindang Hu's gate and smashed it, saying: 'The body is still fine; the sons will suffer.'
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wu's reign Qiang Lian feigned madness; holding a gourd he smashed it at Yuwen Hu's gate, saying: "The body is still fine; the sons will suffer."

sentences.zh: 」時護專政，因朝太后，帝擊殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Hu monopolized government; because of an audience with the empress dowager, the emperor struck and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu monopolized government, the emperor killed him during an audience with the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 發兵捕其諸子，皆備楚毒而死。

translations.literal: Troops were sent to capture his sons; all suffered Chu torture and died.
translations.idiomatic: Troops captured his sons; all died under torture.

sentences.zh: 強練又行乞於市，人或遺之粟麥，輒以無底袋受之。

translations.literal: Qiang Lian also begged in the market; when people gave him grain or wheat he always received it in a bottomless bag.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Lian also begged in the market; when given grain he received it in a bottomless bag.

sentences.zh: 因大笑曰：「盛空。

translations.literal: Therefore laughing loudly he said: 'Full of emptiness.'
translations.idiomatic: Laughing loudly he said: "Full of emptiness."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，周滅，高祖移都，長安城為墟矣。

translations.literal: Before long Zhou perished; Gaozu moved the capital; Chang'an city became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhou fell; Gaozu moved the capital; Chang'an became ruins.

sentences.zh: 開皇六年，霍州有老翁，化為猛獸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaihuang, in Huozhou an old man transformed into a fierce beast.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang year 6, in Huozhou an old man transformed into a fierce beast.

sentences.zh: 七年，相州有桑門，變為蛇，尾繞樹而自抽，長二丈許。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, in Xiangzhou a monk transformed into a snake; its tail coiled around a tree and pulled itself out, more than two zhang long.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, in Xiangzhou a monk transformed into a snake; its tail coiled around a tree and pulled itself free, more than two zhang long.

sentences.zh: 仁壽四年，有人長數丈，見於應門，其跡長四尺五寸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Renshou, a man several zhang tall was seen at the Ying Gate; his tracks were four chi five inches long.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou year 4, a man several zhang tall appeared at the Ying Gate; his tracks were four chi five inches long.

sentences.zh: 其年帝崩。

translations.literal: That year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 大業元年，雁門人房回安，母年百歲，額上生角，長二寸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daye, Fang Huian of Yanmen—his mother a hundred years old—horns grew on her forehead, two inches long.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 1, Fang Huian of Yanmen's hundred-year-old mother grew horns on her forehead, two inches long.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「婦人，陰象也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Woman is the yin image.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Woman is the yin image."

sentences.zh: 角，兵象也。

translations.literal: Horn is the warfare image.
translations.idiomatic: Horn is the image of warfare.

sentences.zh: 下反上之應。

translations.literal: The response of the lower rebelling against the upper.
translations.idiomatic: The response of the lower rebelling against the upper.

sentences.zh: 」是後天下果大亂，陰戎圍帝於雁門。

translations.literal: Afterward the realm indeed fell into great disorder; the northern barbarians besieged the emperor at Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the realm fell into chaos; northern barbarians besieged the emperor at Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 四年，雁門宋穀村有婦人生一肉卵，大如鬥，埋之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, at Songgu Village in Yanmen a woman bore a fleshy egg as large as a dou; it was buried.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, at Songgu Village in Yanmen a woman bore a fleshy egg as large as a dou and buried it.

sentences.zh: 後數日，所埋處雲霧盡合，從地雷震而上，視之洞穴，失卵所在。

translations.literal: Several days later at the burial place clouds and mist all gathered; thunder shook upward from the earth; looking, there was a cave; the egg was gone.
translations.idiomatic: Days later clouds gathered at the burial site; thunder shook upward from the earth; the egg had vanished from a cave.

sentences.zh: 六年，趙郡李來王家婢產一物，大如卵。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, a maid of Li Laizhu of Zhao Commandery bore a thing as large as an egg.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, a maid of Li Laizhu in Zhao Commandery bore a thing as large as an egg.

sentences.zh: 六年正月朔旦，有盜衣白練裙襦，手持香花，自稱彌勒佛出世。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the sixth year, a thief in white silk skirt and jacket, holding incense and flowers, called himself Maitreya Buddha incarnate.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of year 6, a man in white silk, holding incense and flowers, proclaimed himself Maitreya Buddha incarnate.

sentences.zh: 入建國門，奪衛士仗，將為亂。

translations.literal: He entered Jianguo Gate, seized guards' weapons, and was about to raise disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Jianguo Gate, seized guards' weapons, and was about to rebel.

sentences.zh: 齊王暕遇而斬之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Yang encountered and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi Yang encountered and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 後三年，楊玄感作亂，引兵圍洛陽，戰敗伏誅。

translations.literal: Three years later Yang Xuangan raised rebellion, led troops to besiege Luoyang, was defeated in battle and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later Yang Xuangan rebelled, besieged Luoyang, was defeated and executed.

sentences.zh: 八年，有澄公者，若狂人，於東都大叫唱賊。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, there was Master Cheng who, like a madman, at the Eastern Capital loudly cried 'Bandits!'
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, Master Cheng, like a madman, at the Eastern Capital loudly cried "Bandits!"

sentences.zh: 帝聞而惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and hated it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and hated it.

sentences.zh: 明年，玄感舉兵，圍洛陽。

translations.literal: The next year Xuangan raised troops and besieged Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Xuangan raised troops and besieged Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 十二年，澄公又叫賊。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Master Cheng again cried 'Bandits!'
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, Master Cheng again cried "Bandits!"

sentences.zh: 李密逼東都，孟讓燒豐都市而去。

translations.literal: Li Mi pressed the Eastern Capital; Meng Rang burned Fengdu Market and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi pressed the Eastern Capital; Meng Rang burned Fengdu Market and departed.

sentences.zh: 九年，帝在高陽。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the emperor was at Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 the emperor was at Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 唐縣人宋子賢，善為幻術。

translations.literal: Song Zixian of Tang County was skilled in illusion.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zixian of Tang County was skilled in illusion.

sentences.zh: 每夜，樓上有光明，能變作佛形，自稱彌勒出世。

translations.literal: Every night there was light on the tower; he could transform into Buddha form and called himself Maitreya incarnate.
translations.idiomatic: Every night light appeared on his tower; he transformed into Buddha form and called himself Maitreya incarnate.

sentences.zh: 又懸大鏡於堂上，紙素上畫為蛇為獸及人形。

translations.literal: Also he hung a great mirror in the hall; on paper silk he painted snakes, beasts, and human forms.
translations.idiomatic: He hung a great mirror in the hall; on paper he painted snakes, beasts, and human forms.

sentences.zh: 有人來禮謁者，轉側其鏡，遣觀來生形像。

translations.literal: When people came to pay respects, he turned the mirror and had them observe their next-life image.
translations.idiomatic: When people came to worship, he turned the mirror to show their next-life image.

sentences.zh: 或映見紙上蛇形，子賢輒告雲：「此罪業也，當更禮念。

translations.literal: Sometimes the mirror reflected a snake form on the paper; Zixian would tell them: 'This is karmic sin; you should worship again.'
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the mirror showed a snake on the paper; Zixian would say: "This is karmic sin; worship again."

sentences.zh: 」又令禮謁，乃轉人形示之。

translations.literal: Again he had them worship and then turned to show human form.
translations.idiomatic: He had them worship again and then showed human form.

sentences.zh: 遠近惑信，日數百千人。

translations.literal: Near and far were deluded and believed; several hundred or thousand people daily.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far were deceived; hundreds or thousands came daily.

sentences.zh: 遂潛謀作亂，將為無遮佛會，因舉兵，欲襲擊乘輿。

translations.literal: He then secretly plotted rebellion; about to hold a Boundless Buddha Assembly; thereby raising troops, intending to attack the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly plotted rebellion, planning a Boundless Buddha Assembly to raise troops and attack the emperor.

sentences.zh: 事泄，鷹揚郎將以兵捕之。

translations.literal: The matter was exposed; an Eagle-Flying Commandant captured him with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The plot was exposed; an Eagle-Flying Commandant captured him with troops.

sentences.zh: 夜至其所，繞其所居，但見火坑，兵不敢進。

translations.literal: At night arriving at his place, surrounding his dwelling, they only saw a fire pit; troops dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: At night troops surrounded his dwelling but saw only a fire pit and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 郎將曰：「此地素無坑，止妖妄耳。

translations.literal: The commandant said: 'This place normally has no pit; only demonic delusion.'
translations.idiomatic: The commandant said: "This place normally has no pit—only demonic delusion."

sentences.zh: 」及進，無複火矣。

translations.literal: When they advanced, there was no more fire.
translations.idiomatic: When they advanced, the fire was gone.

sentences.zh: 遂擒斬之，並坐其党與千餘家。

translations.literal: They then captured and beheaded him, and more than a thousand of his followers were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: They captured and beheaded him; more than a thousand followers were implicated.

sentences.zh: 其後複有桑門向海明，於扶風自稱彌勒佛出世，潛謀逆亂。

translations.literal: Afterward again there was the monk Xiang Haiming at Fufeng who called himself Maitreya incarnate and secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the monk Xiang Haiming at Fufeng proclaimed himself Maitreya and secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 人有歸心者，輒獲吉夢。

translations.literal: Those who gave him their hearts always received auspicious dreams.
translations.idiomatic: Those who joined him always received auspicious dreams.

sentences.zh: 由是人皆惑之，三輔之士，翕然稱為大聖。

translations.literal: Therefore everyone was deluded; scholars of the three auxiliaries all called him Great Sage.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was deceived; scholars of the three auxiliaries called him Great Sage.

sentences.zh: 因舉兵反，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: He then raised troops in rebellion; the multitude reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He raised troops; his forces reached tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 官軍擊破之。

translations.literal: Government troops defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops defeated him.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「妖言動眾者，茲謂不信。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Demonic words moving the multitude—this is called not believing.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Demonic words moving the multitude—this is called disbelief."

sentences.zh: 路無人行。

translations.literal: No one travels the roads.
translations.idiomatic: No one travels the roads.

sentences.zh: 不出三年，起兵。

translations.literal: Within three years troops will rise.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years troops will rise.

sentences.zh: 」自是天下大亂，路無人行。

translations.literal: From this the realm fell into great disorder; no one traveled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: From this the realm fell into chaos; no one traveled the roads.

sentences.zh: 木金水火沴土梁天監五年十一月，京師地震，木金水火沴土也。

translations.literal: Wood, metal, water, and fire harming earth—in the eleventh month of the fifth year of Tianjian of Liang, the capital earthquake; wood, metal, water, and fire harming earth.
translations.idiomatic: Wood, metal, water, and fire overcoming earth: In the eleventh month of Liang's Tianjian year 5, the capital quaked—wood, metal, water, and fire overcoming earth.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「臣下盛，將動而為害。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Ministers below flourish; about to move and become harmful.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "When ministers below flourish, they will move and bring harm."

sentences.zh: 」京房《易飛候》曰：「地動以冬十一月者，其邑饑亡。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Earth quaking in the eleventh month of winter—that city will hunger and perish.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Earth quaking in winter's eleventh month—that city will hunger and perish."

sentences.zh: 」時交州刺史李凱舉兵反。

translations.literal: At that time Jiao Province Inspector Li Kai raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jiao Province Inspector Li Kai raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 明年，霜，歲儉人饑。

translations.literal: The next year there was frost; the year was lean and people hungered.
translations.idiomatic: The following year frost came; the harvest failed and people starved.

sentences.zh: 普通三年正月，建康地震。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Putong, Jiankang earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Putong year 3, Jiankang quaked.

sentences.zh: 是時，義州刺史文僧朗以州叛。

translations.literal: At that time Yizhou Inspector Wen Senglang rebelled with his province.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yizhou Inspector Wen Senglang rebelled with his province.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月，地震。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year, earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of year 6, earthquake.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「地冬動有音，以十二月者，其邑有行兵。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Earth quaking in winter with sound—in the twelfth month that city will have marching troops.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Earth quaking in winter with sound—in the twelfth month that city will see marching troops."

sentences.zh: 」是時，帝令豫章王琮將兵北伐。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor ordered Prince of Yuzhang Cong to lead troops on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince Yuzhang Cong to lead a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 中大通五年正月，建康地震。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year of Zhongdatong, Jiankang earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhongdatong year 5, Jiankang quaked.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「地以春動，歲不昌。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Earth quaking in spring—the year will not flourish.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Earth quaking in spring—the year will not flourish."

sentences.zh: 」是歲，大水，百姓饑饉。

translations.literal: That year great flood; the common people hungered.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought great flood; the people starved.

sentences.zh: 大同三年十一月，建康地震。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Datong, Jiankang earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Datong year 3, Jiankang quaked.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「地震以十一月，邑有大喪及饑亡。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Earthquake in the eleventh month—the city will have great mourning and hunger and perish.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Earthquake in the eleventh month—the city will suffer great mourning, hunger, and perish."

sentences.zh: 」明年，霜為災，百姓饑。

translations.literal: The next year frost was a disaster; the common people hungered.
translations.idiomatic: The following year frost destroyed crops; the people starved.

sentences.zh: 三年十月，建康地震。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year, Jiankang earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 3, Jiankang quaked.

sentences.zh: 是歲，會稽山賊起。

translations.literal: That year bandits rose on Mount Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: That year bandits rose on Mount Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，建康地震。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year, Jiankang earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 7, Jiankang quaked.

sentences.zh: 是歲，交州人李賁舉兵，逐刺史蕭諮。

translations.literal: That year a man of Jiaozhou, Li Bin, raised troops and drove out Inspector Xiao Zi.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Bin of Jiaozhou raised troops and drove out Inspector Xiao Zi.

sentences.zh: 九年閏正月，地震。

translations.literal: In the intercalary first month of the ninth year, earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary first month of year 9, earthquake.

sentences.zh: 李賁自稱皇帝，署置百官。

translations.literal: Li Bin called himself emperor and established officials.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bin proclaimed himself emperor and established officials.

sentences.zh: 太清三年四月，建康地再震。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Taiqing, Jiankang quaked twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Taiqing year 3, Jiankang quaked twice.

sentences.zh: 時侯景自為大丞相、錄尚書事，帝所須不給。

translations.literal: At that time Hou Jing made himself Grand Chancellor and Chief Minister; what the emperor needed was not supplied.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hou Jing made himself Grand Chancellor; the emperor's needs went unmet.

sentences.zh: 是月，以憂憤崩。

translations.literal: That month, from worry and anger the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That month the emperor died of worry and anger.

sentences.zh: 陳永定二年五月，建康地震。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Yongding of Chen, Jiankang earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Chen's Yongding year 2, Jiankang quaked.

sentences.zh: 時王琳立蕭莊於郢州。

translations.literal: At that time Wang Lin established Xiao Zhuang at Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wang Lin established Xiao Zhuang at Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太建四年十一月，地震。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Taijian, earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Taijian year 4, earthquake.

sentences.zh: 陳寶應反閩中。

translations.literal: Chen Baoying rebelled in Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baoying rebelled in Minzhong.

sentences.zh: 禎明元年正月，地震。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Zhenming, earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhenming year 1, earthquake.

sentences.zh: 施文慶、沈客卿專恣之應也。

translations.literal: The response of Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing acting arbitrarily.
translations.idiomatic: The response to Shi Wenqing and Shen Keqing acting arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 東魏武定二年十一月，西河地陷而且燃。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Wuding of Eastern Wei, Xihe land sank and moreover burned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Eastern Wei's Wuding year 2, Xihe land sank and burned.

sentences.zh: 京房《易妖占》曰：「地自陷，其君亡。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yiyaozhan says: 'When earth sinks by itself, its ruler perishes.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yiyaozhan says: "When earth sinks by itself, its ruler perishes."

sentences.zh: 」祖釭曰：「火，陽精也；

translations.literal: Zu Geng said: 'Fire is the essence of yang;'
translations.idiomatic: Zu Geng said: "Fire is the essence of yang;"

sentences.zh: 地者，陰主也。

translations.literal: Earth is yin's master.
translations.idiomatic: earth is yin's master.

sentences.zh: 地燃，越陰之道，行陽之政，臣下擅恣，終以自害。

translations.literal: Earth burning crosses yin's way and practices yang's governance; ministers below act arbitrarily and ultimately harm themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Burning earth crosses yin's way and practices yang's governance; ministers act arbitrarily and ultimately destroy themselves.

sentences.zh: 」時後齊神武作宰，而侯景專擅河南。

translations.literal: At that time Northern Qi's Shenwu served as chief minister, while Hou Jing monopolized Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi's Gao Huan served as chief minister while Hou Jing monopolized Henan.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，神武果崩，景遂作亂，而自取敗亡之應。

translations.literal: Two years later Shenwu indeed died; Jing then raised disorder—the response of self-defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Gao Huan died; Jing rebelled—the omen of self-defeat fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 後齊河清二年，并州地震。

translations.literal: In the second year of Heqing of Northern Qi, Bingzhou earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi's Heqing year 2, Bingzhou quaked.

sentences.zh: 和士開專恣之應。

translations.literal: The response of He Shikai acting arbitrarily.
translations.idiomatic: The response to He Shikai acting arbitrarily.

sentences.zh: 後周建德二年，涼州地頻震。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande of Later Zhou, Liangzhou land frequently quaked.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Zhou's Jiande year 2, Liangzhou frequently quaked.

sentences.zh: 城郭多壞，地裂出泉。

translations.literal: City walls mostly ruined; the earth split and springs emerged.
translations.idiomatic: City walls mostly collapsed; the earth split and springs emerged.

sentences.zh: 京房《易妖占》曰：「地分裂，羌夷叛。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yiyaozhan says: 'Earth splitting—Qiang and barbarians rebel.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yiyaozhan says: "When earth splits, Qiang and barbarians rebel."

sentences.zh: 」時吐谷渾頻寇河西。

translations.literal: At that time Tuyuhun frequently raided Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tuyuhun frequently raided Hexi.

sentences.zh: 開皇十四年五月，京師地震。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourteenth year of Kaihuang, the capital earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaihuang year 14, the capital quaked.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「地動以夏五月，人流亡。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Earth quaking in the fifth month of summer—people flee.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Earth quaking in summer's fifth month—people flee."

sentences.zh: 」是歲關中饑，帝令百姓就糧于關東。

translations.literal: That year Guanzhong hungered; the emperor ordered the people to seek grain in Guandong.
translations.idiomatic: That year Guanzhong starved; the emperor sent people to seek grain in Guandong.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年四月，岐、雍地震。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Renshou, Qi and Yong earthquake.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Renshou year 2, Qi and Yong quaked.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「地動以夏四月，五穀不熟，人大饑。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'Earth quaking in the fourth month of summer—the five grains do not ripen; people greatly hunger.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "Earth quaking in summer's fourth month—crops fail and people starve."

sentences.zh: 三年，梁州就穀山崩。

translations.literal: In the third year, at Jiugu Mountain in Liangzhou a mountain collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 3, Jiugu Mountain in Liangzhou collapsed.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「崩散落，背叛不事上之類也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Collapse and scattering—the kind that rebels and does not serve superiors.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Collapse and scattering symbolize rebellion against superiors."

sentences.zh: 」梁州為漢地。

translations.literal: Liangzhou is Han territory.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou was Han territory.

sentences.zh: 明年，漢王諒舉兵反。

translations.literal: The next year Prince of Han Liang raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Prince Han Liang raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 大業七年，砥柱山崩，壅河，逆流數十里。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daye, Mount Dizhu collapsed, blocking the river; the current reversed for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 7, Mount Dizhu collapsed, blocking the river; the current reversed for tens of li.

sentences.zh: 劉向《洪範五行傳》曰：「山者，君之象；

translations.literal: Liu Xiang's Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Mountain is the ruler's image;'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang's Wuxing Commentary says: "Mountain is the ruler's image;"

sentences.zh: 水者，陰之表，人之類也。

translations.literal: Water is yin's manifestation, the kind of people.
translations.idiomatic: water is yin's manifestation, the kind of people.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，君人擁威重，將崩壞，百姓不得其所。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the ruler holding heavy authority will collapse and ruin; the common people will not have their place.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the ruler holding heavy authority will collapse; the people will lose their place.

sentences.zh: 」時帝興遼東之師，百姓不堪其役，四海怨叛。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor raised Liaodong armies; the common people could not bear the corvée; the four seas rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raised Liaodong armies; the people could not bear the corvée; the realm rebelled.

sentences.zh: 帝不能悟，卒以滅亡。

translations.literal: The emperor could not understand; in the end he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor failed to understand; in the end he was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「皇之不極，是謂不建。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'When the sovereign does not reach the extreme, this is called not establishing.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "When the sovereign fails to reach the extreme, it is called failure to establish."

sentences.zh: 厥咎瞀，厥罰常陰，厥極弱。

translations.literal: Its fault is confusion; its punishment is constant yin; its extreme is weakness.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is confusion; the penalty is constant yin; the ultimate consequence is weakness.

sentences.zh: 時則有射妖，則有龍蛇之孽，則有馬禍。

translations.literal: At such times there are shooting demons; there are dragon-and-snake calamities; there are horse portents.
translations.idiomatic: In such seasons shooting demons appear, dragon-and-snake calamities arise, and horse omens manifest.

sentences.zh: 」雲陰開皇二十年十月，久陰不雨。

translations.literal: Cloud yin—in the tenth month of the twentieth year of Kaihuang, prolonged yin without rain.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud yin: In the tenth month of Kaihuang year 20, prolonged overcast without rain.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「王者失中，臣下強盛而蔽君明，則雲陰。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: 'When the king loses the center, ministers below are strong and flourishing and obscure the ruler's clarity—then cloud yin.'
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang said: "When the king loses the center and powerful ministers obscure his clarity, yin clouds appear."

sentences.zh: 」是時，獨孤後遂與楊素陰譖太子勇，廢為庶人。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dugu then with Yang Su secretly slandered Crown Prince Yong and deposed him as commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dugu with Yang Su secretly slandered Crown Prince Yong and deposed him.

sentences.zh: 射妖東魏武定四年，後齊神武作宰，親率諸軍，攻西魏於玉壁。

translations.literal: Shooting demon—in the fourth year of Wuding of Eastern Wei, Northern Qi's Shenwu served as chief minister and personally led the armies attacking Western Wei at Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: Shooting demon: In Eastern Wei's Wuding year 4, Gao Huan personally led armies attacking Western Wei at Yubi.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，帝不豫，班師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year the emperor was unwell and withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he fell ill and withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 將士震懼，皆曰：「韋孝寬以定功弩射殺丞相。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers were fearful; all said: 'Wei Xiaokuan with a fixed-power crossbow shot and killed the chief minister.'
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers feared: "Wei Xiaokuan's crossbow killed the chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」西魏下令國中曰：「勁弩一發，凶身自殞。

translations.literal: Western Wei issued an order in the state: 'A powerful crossbow one shot—the villain's body perishes by itself.'
translations.idiomatic: Western Wei proclaimed: "One shot from a powerful crossbow—the villain perishes."

sentences.zh: 」神武聞而惡之，其疾暴增，近射妖也。

translations.literal: Shenwu heard and hated it; his illness sharply increased—close to shooting demon.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan heard and hated it; his illness sharply worsened—a shooting demon omen.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「射者，兵戎禍亂之象，氣逆天則禍亂將起。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Shooting is the image of warfare and disorder; qi opposing Heaven then disorder will rise.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Shooting symbolizes warfare and disorder; when qi opposes Heaven, chaos rises."

sentences.zh: 」神武行，殿中將軍曹魏祖諫曰：「王以死氣逆生氣，為客不利，主人則可。

translations.literal: Shenwu was going; Palace Guard General Wei Caizu remonstrated: 'The king with death-qi opposes life-qi; as guest it is unfavorable; as host it is acceptable.'
translations.idiomatic: Palace Guard Wei Caizu remonstrated: "Your death-qi opposes life-qi; as attacker you are disadvantaged; as defender you prevail."

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，頓軍五旬，頻戰沮衄。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow; the army halted fifty days; battles frequently failed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused; the army halted fifty days; battles repeatedly failed.

sentences.zh: 又聽孤虛之言，於城北斷汾水，起土山。

translations.literal: Also listening to guxu words, at the north of the city the Fen River was cut off and an earthen mountain raised.
translations.idiomatic: Heeding empty divination, he cut off the Fen River north of the city and raised an earthen mountain.

sentences.zh: 其處天險千餘尺，功竟不就，死者七萬。

translations.literal: That place was a natural barrier more than a thousand chi; the work ultimately did not succeed; seventy thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: That natural barrier stood more than a thousand chi high; the work failed; seventy thousand died.

sentences.zh: 氣逆天之咎也。

translations.literal: The fault of qi opposing Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The fault of qi opposing Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其年帝崩。

translations.literal: That year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 明年，王思政擾河南。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Si'zheng disturbed Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Si'zheng disturbed Henan.

sentences.zh: 武平，後主自并州還鄴，至八公嶺，夜與左右歌而行。

translations.literal: During Wuping, Houzhu returned from Bingzhou to Ye; reaching Bagong Ridge, at night he sang with his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: During Wuping, Houzhu returned from Bingzhou to Ye; at Bagong Ridge he sang with attendants at night.

sentences.zh: 有一人忽發狂，意後主以為狐媚，伏草中彎弓而射之。

translations.literal: One man suddenly went mad; thinking Houzhu was a fox demon, he crouched in the grass, bent his bow and shot at him.
translations.idiomatic: One man suddenly went mad, thinking Houzhu a fox demon; he crouched in the grass and shot at him.

sentences.zh: 傷數人，幾中後主。

translations.literal: Several people were wounded; he nearly hit Houzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Several were wounded; he nearly hit Houzhu.

sentences.zh: 後主執而斬之。

translations.literal: Houzhu seized and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu seized and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 其人不自覺也。

translations.literal: The man himself was not aware.
translations.idiomatic: The man himself was unaware.

sentences.zh: 狐而能媚，獸之妖妄也。

translations.literal: Foxes able to bewitch—the demonic delusion of beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Foxes able to bewitch—the demonic delusion of beasts.

sentences.zh: 時帝不恤國政，專與內人閹豎酣歌為樂。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor did not care for state affairs; exclusively with inner people and eunuchs he drank and sang for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor neglected state affairs, drinking and singing with concubines and eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 或衣襤縷衣，行乞為娛。

translations.literal: Sometimes wearing tattered clothes, going begging for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he wore tattered clothes and begged for amusement.

sentences.zh: 此妖妄之象。

translations.literal: This is the image of demonic delusion.
translations.idiomatic: This was the image of demonic delusion.

sentences.zh: 人又射之，兵戎禍亂之應也。

translations.literal: People again shooting at him—the response of warfare and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: People shooting at him—the response of warfare and disorder.

sentences.zh: 未幾而國滅。

translations.literal: Before long the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the state perished.

sentences.zh: 龍蛇之孽梁天監二年，北梁州潭中有龍鬥，濆霧數裡。

translations.literal: Dragon-and-snake calamity—in the second year of Tianjian of Liang, in a pool in North Liangzhou dragons fought; mist sprayed for several li.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-and-snake calamity: In Liang's Tianjian year 2, dragons fought in a pool in North Liangzhou; mist sprayed for several li.

sentences.zh: 龍蛇之孽。

translations.literal: Dragon-and-snake calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon-and-snake calamity.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「龍，獸之難害者也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Dragon is among beasts hard to harm.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "The dragon is among beasts the hardest to harm."

sentences.zh: 天之類，君之象。

translations.literal: Heaven's kind; the ruler's image.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's kind; the ruler's image.

sentences.zh: 天氣害，君道傷，則龍亦害。

translations.literal: When Heaven's qi is harmed, the ruler's way is injured—then dragons are also harmed.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven's qi is harmed and the ruler's way injured, dragons too are harmed.

sentences.zh: 鬥者兵革之象也。

translations.literal: Fighting is the image of armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting is the image of armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 」京房《易飛候》曰：「眾心不安，厥妖龍鬥。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: 'When the multitude's hearts are unsettled, its anomaly is dragons fighting.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Yifeihou says: "When the multitude's hearts are unsettled, dragons fight."

sentences.zh: 」是時帝初即位，而有陳伯之、劉季連之亂，國內危懼。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had newly ascended; there were the disorders of Chen Bozhi and Liu Jilian; within the state there was fear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had newly ascended; disorders of Chen Bozhi and Liu Jilian arose; fear spread within the state.

sentences.zh: 普通五年六月，龍鬥于曲阿王陂，因西行，至建陵城，所經之處，樹木皆折開數十丈。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year of Putong, dragons fought at Wangpo in Qu'a; then going west, reaching Jianling city; wherever they passed, trees were snapped open for several tens of zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Putong year 5, dragons fought at Wangpo in Qu'a, then went west to Jianling; wherever they passed, trees snapped open for tens of zhang.

sentences.zh: 與天監二年同占。

translations.literal: Same omen as the second year of Tianjian.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as Tianjian year 2.

sentences.zh: 經建陵而樹木折者，國有兵革之禍，園陵殘毀之象。

translations.literal: Passing Jianling and trees snapping—the state's having warfare calamity; imperial gardens and tombs ruined—the image.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Jianling and snapping trees foretold warfare and the ruin of imperial gardens and tombs.

sentences.zh: 時帝專以講論為務，不崇耕戰，將輕而卒惰。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor exclusively used lectures as his task, did not esteem farming and warfare; generals were light and soldiers lazy.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor devoted himself to lectures, neglected farming and warfare; generals were lax and soldiers idle.

sentences.zh: 君道既傷，故有龍孽之應。

translations.literal: The ruler's way already injured—therefore the response of dragon calamity.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's way was injured—hence the dragon calamity.

sentences.zh: 帝殊不悟。

translations.literal: The emperor especially did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor especially failed to understand.

sentences.zh: 至太清元年，黎州水中又有龍鬥。

translations.literal: Reaching the first year of Taiqing, in the waters of Lizhou again dragons fought.
translations.idiomatic: By Taiqing year 1, dragons again fought in the waters of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 波浪湧起，雲霧四合，而見白龍南走，黑龍隨之。

translations.literal: Waves surged; clouds and mist gathered on four sides; a white dragon was seen going south; a black dragon followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Waves surged; clouds gathered; a white dragon went south; a black dragon followed.

sentences.zh: 其年，侯景以兵來降，帝納之而無備，國人皆懼。

translations.literal: That year Hou Jing came with troops to surrender; the emperor received him without preparation; everyone in the state was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: That year Hou Jing surrendered with troops; the emperor received him unprepared; the state was afraid.

sentences.zh: 俄而難作，帝以憂崩。

translations.literal: Before long calamity arose; the emperor died of worry.
translations.idiomatic: Before long calamity arose; the emperor died of worry.

sentences.zh: 大同十年夏，有龍夜因雷而墮延陵人家井中，明旦視之，大如驢。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year of Datong, at night a dragon fell into a Yanling commoner's well due to thunder; the next morning looking at it, it was as large as a donkey.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Datong year 10, at night thunder caused a dragon to fall into a Yanling commoner's well; by morning it was as large as a donkey.

sentences.zh: 將以戟刺之，俄見庭中及室中各有大蛇，如數百斛船，家人奔走。

translations.literal: About to stab it with a halberd; suddenly in the courtyard and rooms there were each great snakes like ships of several hundred hu; the family fled.
translations.idiomatic: About to stab it with a halberd, great snakes like ships of several hundred hu appeared in courtyard and rooms; the family fled.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「龍，陽類，貴象也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Dragon is yang kind, the image of the noble.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Dragon is yang kind, the image of the noble."

sentences.zh: 上則在天，下則在地，不當見庶人邑裡室家。

translations.literal: Above it is in heaven; below it is on earth—it should not be seen in common people's neighborhoods and homes.
translations.idiomatic: Above in heaven, below on earth—it should not appear in common people's homes.

sentences.zh: 井中，幽深之象也，諸侯且有幽執之禍，皇不建之咎也。

translations.literal: In a well is the image of depth; feudal lords will have the calamity of secret imprisonment; the fault of the sovereign not establishing.
translations.idiomatic: A well symbolizes depth; feudal lords would suffer secret imprisonment—the sovereign's failure to establish.

sentences.zh: 」後侯景反，果幽殺簡文於酒庫，宗室王侯皆幽死。

translations.literal: Afterward Hou Jing rebelled; indeed he secretly killed Jianwen in the wine storehouse; royal clan princes and marquises were all secretly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing rebelled; he secretly killed Jianwen in the wine storehouse; royal princes were all secretly killed.

sentences.zh: 陳太建十一年正月，龍見南兗州池中，與梁大同十年同占。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year of Taijian of Chen, a dragon was seen in a pool in Southern Yanzhou—same omen as the tenth year of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chen's Taijian year 11, a dragon appeared in a pool in Southern Yanzhou—the same portent as Datong year 10.

sentences.zh: 未幾，後主嗣位，驕淫荒怠，動不得中。

translations.literal: Before long Houzhu succeeded; arrogant, debauched, negligent, acting without the center.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Houzhu succeeded—arrogant, debauched, negligent, acting without balance.

sentences.zh: 其後竟以國亡，身被幽執。

translations.literal: Afterward he was indeed destroyed with the state; personally suffered secret imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: He was destroyed with the state and personally suffered imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 東魏武定元年，有大蛇見武牢城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuding of Eastern Wei, a great snake was seen at Wulao city.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Wei's Wuding year 1, a great snake appeared at Wulao city.

sentences.zh: 是時，北豫州刺史高仲密妻李氏，慧而豔。

translations.literal: At that time the wife of Beiyu Prefect Gao Zhongmi, Lady Li, was clever and lovely.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Beiyu Prefect Gao Zhongmi's wife Lady Li was clever and lovely.

sentences.zh: 世子澄悅之，仲密內不自安，遂以武牢叛，陰引西魏，大戰于河陽。

translations.literal: Heir Apparent Cheng was pleased with her; Zhongmi was inwardly uneasy; therefore he rebelled with Wulao, secretly leading in Western Wei; a great battle at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Heir Apparent Cheng desired her; Zhongmi rebelled at Wulao, secretly leading Western Wei; a great battle at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 神武為西兵所窘，僅而獲免，死者數千。

translations.literal: Shenwu was cornered by Western troops; barely escaped; several thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was cornered by Western troops; barely escaped; several thousand died.

sentences.zh: 後齊天保九年，有龍長七八丈，見齊州大堂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao of Northern Qi, there was a dragon seven or eight zhang long seen in the great hall of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Qi's Tianbao year 9, a dragon seven or eight zhang long appeared in Qi Province's great hall.

sentences.zh: 占同大同十年。

translations.literal: Same omen as the tenth year of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as Datong year 10.

sentences.zh: 時常山、長廣二王權重，帝不思抑損。

translations.literal: At that time the Princes of Changshan and Changuang were weighty in power; the emperor did not think to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Changshan and Changuang held great power; the emperor failed to restrain them.

sentences.zh: 明年帝崩，太子殷嗣立。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor died; Crown Prince Yin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor died; Crown Prince Yin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 常山王演果廢帝為濟南王，幽而害之。

translations.literal: Prince of Changshan Yan indeed deposed the emperor as Prince of Jinan, imprisoned and harmed him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Changshan Yan deposed the emperor as Prince Jinan, imprisoned and killed him.

sentences.zh: 河清元年，龍見濟州浴堂中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Heqing, a dragon was seen in the bath hall of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Heqing year 1, a dragon appeared in Jizhou's bath hall.

sentences.zh: 占同天保九年。

translations.literal: Same omen as the ninth year of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as Tianbao year 9.

sentences.zh: 先是平秦王歸彥受昭帝遺詔，立太子百年為嗣。

translations.literal: Before this Prince of Pingqin Guiyan received Emperor Xiaozhao's testament and established Crown Prince Bainian as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Prince Pingqin Guiyan received Emperor Xiaozhao's testament and established Crown Prince Bainian as successor.

sentences.zh: 而歸彥遂立長廣王湛，是為武成帝。

translations.literal: But Guiyan then established Prince of Changuang Zhan, who was Emperor Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: But Guiyan established Prince Changuang Zhan as Emperor Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 而廢百年為樂陵王，竟以幽死。

translations.literal: And deposed Bainian as Prince of Leling; in the end he was secretly killed.
translations.idiomatic: He deposed Bainian as Prince Leling, who was secretly killed.

sentences.zh: 天統四年，貴鄉人伐枯木，得一黃龍，折腳，死于孔中，齊稱木德。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tiantong, a Gui Township man felling a withered tree obtained a yellow dragon with broken legs; it died in the hole; Qi claimed wood virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiantong year 4, a Gui Township man felling a withered tree found a yellow dragon with broken legs dead in the hole; Qi claimed wood virtue.

sentences.zh: 龍，君象。

translations.literal: Dragon is the ruler's image.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon is the ruler's image.

sentences.zh: 木枯龍死，不祥之甚。

translations.literal: Wood withered and dragon dead—inauspicious to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Wood withered and dragon dead—inauspicious in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 其年武成崩。

translations.literal: That year Wucheng died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wucheng died.

sentences.zh: 武平三年，龍見邯鄲井中，其氣五色屬天。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wuping, a dragon was seen in a Handan well; its qi five-colored reaching heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping year 3, a dragon appeared in a Handan well; five-colored vapor reached heaven.

sentences.zh: 又見汲郡佛寺涸井中。

translations.literal: Also seen in a dried well of a Buddhist temple at Ji Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Also seen in a dried well at a Ji Commandery Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 占同河清元年。

translations.literal: Same omen as the first year of Heqing.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as Heqing year 1.

sentences.zh: 後主竟降周，後被誅。

translations.literal: Houzhu in the end surrendered to Zhou; afterward was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu ultimately surrendered to Zhou and was executed.

sentences.zh: 武平七年，并州招遠樓下，有赤蛇與黑蛇鬥，數日，赤蛇死。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuping, below the Zhaoyuan Tower in Bingzhou, a red snake and black snake fought; after several days the red snake died.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping year 7, below Zhaoyuan Tower in Bingzhou, a red snake and black snake fought; after days the red snake died.

sentences.zh: 赤，齊尚色；

translations.literal: Red is Qi's honored color;
translations.idiomatic: Red was Qi's honored color;

sentences.zh: 黑，周尚色。

translations.literal: Black is Zhou's honored color.
translations.idiomatic: black was Zhou's honored color.

sentences.zh: 鬥而死，滅亡之象也。

translations.literal: Fighting and dying—the image of destruction and perishing.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting until death symbolized destruction.

sentences.zh: 後主任用邪佞，與周師連兵于晉州之下。

translations.literal: Houzhu employed wicked flatterers; with Zhou armies continuously fought below Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu employed wicked flatterers; with Zhou armies he fought below Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 委軍于孽臣高阿那肱，竟啟敵人，皇不建之咎也。

translations.literal: Entrusting the army to the wicked minister Gao Anagai, he ultimately opened to the enemy—the fault of the sovereign not establishing.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted the army to Gao Anagai, who opened to the enemy—the sovereign's failure to establish.

sentences.zh: 後主遂為周師所虜。

translations.literal: Houzhu was then captured by Zhou armies.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu was captured by Zhou armies.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王儼壞北宮中白馬浮圖，石趙時澄公所建。

translations.literal: Prince of Langye Yan destroyed the white horse pagoda in the Northern Palace built by Master Cheng of Stone Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Langye Yan destroyed the white horse pagoda in the Northern Palace built by Master Cheng of Stone Zhao.

sentences.zh: 見白蛇長數丈，迴旋失所在。

translations.literal: A white snake several zhang long was seen circling and then vanished.
translations.idiomatic: A white snake several zhang long was seen circling, then vanished.

sentences.zh: 時儼專誅，失中之咎也。

translations.literal: At that time Yan exclusively executed—the fault of losing the center.
translations.idiomatic: Yan executed exclusively—the fault of losing the center.

sentences.zh: 見變不知戒，以及於難。

translations.literal: Seeing the anomaly and not knowing to be warned, thus reaching calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the omen and failing to heed it, he reached calamity.

sentences.zh: 後周建德五年，黑龍墜於亳州而死。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiande of Later Zhou, a black dragon fell at Bozhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: In Northern Zhou's Jiande year 5, a black dragon fell at Bozhou and died.

sentences.zh: 龍，君之象。

translations.literal: Dragon is the ruler's image.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon is the ruler's image.

sentences.zh: 黑，周所尚色。

translations.literal: Black is the color Zhou honors.
translations.idiomatic: Black was the color Zhou favored.

sentences.zh: 墜而死，不祥之甚。

translations.literal: Falling and dying—inauspicious to the extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Falling and dying—inauspicious in the extreme.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子不才，帝每以為慮，直臣王軌、宇文孝伯等驟請廢立，帝不能用。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince lacked talent; the emperor always worried; upright ministers Wang Gui and Yuwen Xiaobo repeatedly requested deposing and establishing; the emperor could not use them.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince lacked talent; upright ministers Wang Gui and Yuwen Xiaobo repeatedly urged replacement; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 後二歲，帝崩，太子立，虐殺齊王及孝伯等，因而國亡。

translations.literal: Two years later the emperor died; the crown prince established; cruelly killed Prince Qi and Xiaobo and others; thus the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor died; the crown prince established, cruelly killed Prince Qi and Xiaobo—and the state perished.

sentences.zh: 仁壽四年，龍見代州總管府井中。
