translations.literal: In the fourth year of Renshou, a dragon was seen in the well of the General Headquarters at Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Renshou year 4, a dragon appeared in the well at Daizhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 其龍或變為鐵馬甲士彎弓上射之象。

translations.literal: The dragon sometimes transformed into the image of armored iron horsemen bending bows and shooting upward.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon sometimes transformed into armored iron horsemen bending bows and shooting upward.

sentences.zh: 變為鐵馬，近馬禍也。

translations.literal: Transforming into iron horses—close to horse portent.
translations.idiomatic: Transforming into iron horses—close to a horse omen.

sentences.zh: 彎弓上射，又近射妖，諸侯將有兵革之變，以致幽囚也。

translations.literal: Bending bow and shooting upward—also close to shooting demon; feudal lords will have the change of armor and weapons, leading to secret imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: Bending bow and shooting upward—also a shooting omen; feudal lords would face warfare and imprisonment.

sentences.zh: 是時漢王諒潛謀逆亂，故變兵戒之。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Han Liang secretly plotted rebellion; therefore it changed to military warning.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Han Liang secretly plotted rebellion; the omen changed to military warning.

sentences.zh: 諒不悟，遂興兵反，事敗，廢為庶人，幽囚數年而死。

translations.literal: Liang did not understand; then raised troops in rebellion; the matter failed; he was deposed as commoner, secretly imprisoned several years and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liang failed to heed it; he rebelled, failed, was deposed, imprisoned for years, and died.

sentences.zh: 馬禍侯景僭尊號於江南，每將戰，其所乘白馬，長鳴蹀足者輒勝，垂頭者輒不利。

translations.literal: Horse portent—Hou Jing usurped title in Jiangnan; whenever about to battle, the white horse he rode, if it neighed and stamped would win; if it hung its head would be unfavorable.
translations.idiomatic: Horse omen: Hou Jing usurped title in Jiangnan; before battle, if his white horse neighed and stamped he won; if it hung its head he lost.

sentences.zh: 西州之役，馬臥不起，景拜請，且棰之，竟不動。

translations.literal: At the battle of Xizhou the horse lay down and would not rise; Jing bowed and requested, and also beat it—it still did not move.
translations.idiomatic: At Xizhou his horse lay down and would not rise; Jing bowed and beat it—it still would not move.

sentences.zh: 近馬禍也。

translations.literal: Close to horse portent.
translations.idiomatic: This was a horse omen.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「馬者兵象。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Horse is the warfare image.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Horse is the image of warfare."

sentences.zh: 將有寇戎之事，故馬為怪。

translations.literal: About to have bandit and warfare affairs—therefore the horse becomes strange.
translations.idiomatic: When warfare is coming, horses become strange.

sentences.zh: 」景因此大敗。

translations.literal: Jing because of this was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was greatly defeated because of this.

sentences.zh: 陳太建五年，衡州馬生角。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian of Chen, horses at Hengzhou grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen's Taijian year 5, horses at Hengzhou grew horns.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「馬生角，兵之象，敗亡之表也。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Horse growing horns is the image of warfare; the manifestation of defeat and ruin.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Horses growing horns symbolize warfare and foretell defeat."

sentences.zh: 」是時宣帝遣吳明徹出師呂梁，與周師拒。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuan dispatched Wu Mingche to lead armies to Luliang to resist Zhou armies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan dispatched Wu Mingche to Luliang to resist Zhou armies.

sentences.zh: 連兵數歲，眾軍覆沒，明徹竟為周師所虜。

translations.literal: Warfare continued several years; the armies were destroyed; Mingche was captured by Zhou armies.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting continued for years; the armies were destroyed; Mingche was captured.

sentences.zh: 天保中，廣宗有馬，兩耳間生角，如羊尾。

translations.literal: During Tianbao, at Guangzong there was a horse with horns growing between its ears like a sheep's tail.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao, at Guangzong a horse grew horns between its ears like a sheep's tail.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「天子親伐，則馬生角。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Yizhuan says: 'When the Son of Heaven personally campaigns, horses grow horns.'
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary says: "When the Son of Heaven campaigns personally, horses grow horns."

sentences.zh: 」四年，契丹犯塞，文宣帝親禦六軍以擊之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Khitan violated the frontier; Emperor Wenxuan personally led the six armies to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, the Khitan raided the frontier; Emperor Wenxuan personally led six armies against them.

sentences.zh: 大業四年，太原廄馬死者太半，帝怒，遣使案問。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daye, more than half the horses in Taiyuan stables died; the emperor was enraged and sent an envoy to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year 4, more than half the horses in Taiyuan stables died; the emperor sent an envoy to investigate.

sentences.zh: 主者曰：「每夜廄中馬無故自驚，因而致死。

translations.literal: The keeper said: 'Every night the stable horses for no reason startled themselves and thus died.'
translations.idiomatic: The keeper said: "Every night the horses startled themselves for no reason and died."

sentences.zh: 」帝令巫者視之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered shamans to examine it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered shamans to examine it.

sentences.zh: 巫者知帝將有遼東之役，因希旨言曰：「先帝令楊素、史萬歲取之，將鬼兵以伐遼東也。

translations.literal: The shamans, knowing the emperor was about to have a Liaodong campaign, therefore to please him said: 'The former emperor ordered Yang Su and Shi Wansui to take them; they will lead ghost soldiers to campaign in Liaodong.'
translations.idiomatic: The shamans, knowing a Liaodong campaign was coming, flattered him: "The former emperor ordered Yang Su and Shi Wansui to lead ghost soldiers against Liaodong."

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅，因釋主者。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and therefore released the keeper.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and released the keeper.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「逆天氣，故馬多死。

translations.literal: The Hongfan Wuxing Zhuan says: 'Opposing Heaven's qi—therefore many horses die.'
translations.idiomatic: The Wuxing Commentary says: "Opposing Heaven's qi—therefore many horses die."

sentences.zh: 」是時，帝每歲巡幸，北事長城，西通且末，國內虛耗，天戒若曰，除廄馬，無事巡幸。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor every year toured; northern matters were the Great Wall; west connected to Qiemo; within the state was exhausted; Heaven's warning seemed to say: remove stable horses, do not tour without cause.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor toured yearly, built the Great Wall, exhausted the state; Heaven warned: remove the stable horses, cease needless touring.

sentences.zh: 帝不悟，遂至亂。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand; thus reaching disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor failed to understand; disorder followed.

sentences.zh: 十一年，河南、扶風三郡，並有馬生角，長數寸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Henan and Fufeng three commanderies all had horses grow horns several cun long.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11, Henan and Fufeng commanderies all had horses grow horns several cun long.

sentences.zh: 與天保初同占。

translations.literal: Same omen as the beginning of Tianbao.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as the beginning of Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝頻歲親征高麗。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor frequently in person campaigned against Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor frequently campaigned against Goguryeo in person.

sentences.zh: 義甯元年，帝在江都宮，龍廄馬無故而死，旬日，死至數百匹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yining, the emperor was at Jiangdu Palace; dragon stable horses died for no reason; within ten days deaths reached several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In Yining year 1, at Jiangdu Palace dragon stable horses died for no reason; within ten days several hundred died.

sentences.zh: 與大業四年同占。

translations.literal: Same omen as the fourth year of Daye.
translations.idiomatic: The same portent as Daye year 4.
